mis-selling.t: 误导性销售；不当销售行为

e.en: The bank paid compensation for {mis-selling} insurance policies.
e.zh: 这家银行因误导性销售保险产品而支付了赔偿。

e.en: Regulators are investigating widespread {mis-selling} in the pension market.
e.zh: 监管机构正在调查养老金市场中普遍存在的不当销售行为。

e.en: The warehouse system can {mis-sort} packages with damaged labels.
e.zh: 仓库系统可能会把标签损坏的包裹分拣错。

e.en: A small coding bug caused the app to {mis-sort} the results.
e.zh: 一个小的代码错误导致应用把结果排序分错。

e.en: One {mis-spelling} can make the address impossible to find.
e.zh: 一个拼写错误就可能让地址无法找到。

e.en: The teacher circled each {mis-spelling} in red ink.
e.zh: 老师用红笔圈出了每一个误拼的词。

e.en: The report may {mis-state} the company's actual profits.
e.zh: 这份报告可能错误陈述了公司的实际利润。

e.en: Please do not {mis-state} my position in the meeting.
e.zh: 请不要在会议上歪曲我的立场。

e.en: The auditor found a serious {mis-statement} in the accounts.
e.zh: 审计员在账目中发现了一处严重的错误陈述。

e.en: Her lawyer argued that the {mis-statement} was accidental.
e.zh: 她的律师辩称那项虚假陈述并非故意。

mis-time.t: 时间安排不当；时机选错

e.en: If you {mis-time} the jump, you will miss the platform.
e.zh: 如果你起跳时机选错，就会错过那个平台。

e.en: The company badly {mis-timed} its product launch.
e.zh: 这家公司严重选错了产品发布的时机。

e.en: A careless {mis-translation} changed the meaning of the contract.
e.zh: 一次粗心的误译改变了合同的含义。

e.en: The joke disappeared because of a {mis-translation}.
e.zh: 这个笑话因为翻译错误而完全失去了效果。

e.en: Several {mis-translations} confused the foreign visitors.
e.zh: 几处误译让外国访客感到困惑。

e.en: The new edition corrected many old {mis-translations}.
e.zh: 新版纠正了许多旧版本中的翻译错误。

e.en: There was a simple {mis-understanding} about the meeting time.
e.zh: 关于会议时间出现了一个简单的误会。

e.en: His silence led to a serious {mis-understanding}.
e.zh: 他的沉默导致了一场严重的误解。

e.en: Clear notes can prevent {mis-understandings} after the call.
e.zh: 清楚的记录可以避免通话后的误会。

e.en: Most of their arguments came from small {mis-understandings}.
e.zh: 他们的大多数争吵都源于小小的误解。

e.en: People often {mis-use} technical terms in casual conversation.
e.zh: 人们在日常谈话中常常误用技术术语。

e.en: The policy aims to prevent the {mis-use} of personal data.
e.zh: 这项政策旨在防止个人数据被滥用。

e.en: An officer who {misacts} may face formal discipline.
e.zh: 行为不当的官员可能会面临正式处分。

e.en: The old rule punished servants who {misact} in public.
e.zh: 这条旧规会惩罚在公共场合举止失当的仆人。

misadjusted.t: 调节不当的；调整错误的

e.en: A {misadjusted} brake can make the bicycle unsafe.
e.zh: 调节不当的刹车会让自行车变得不安全。

e.en: The machine failed because one valve was {misadjusted}.
e.zh: 机器故障是因为一个阀门调整错误。

e.en: The mechanic found a slight {misadjustment} in the steering system.
e.zh: 机械师发现转向系统有轻微的调节不当。

e.en: Even a small {misadjustment} can affect the sensor reading.
e.zh: 即使很小的调整错误也会影响传感器读数。

e.en: The inquiry blamed years of {misadministration} for the hospital's problems.
e.zh: 调查将医院的问题归咎于多年的管理不善。

e.en: Citizens complained about corruption and {misadministration}.
e.zh: 市民抱怨腐败和行政失当。

misadventurous.t: 倒霉多险的；不幸冒险的

e.en: Their {misadventurous} journey ended with a broken boat.
e.zh: 他们这趟倒霉多险的旅程以船只损坏告终。

e.en: The novel follows a {misadventurous} young sailor.
e.zh: 这部小说讲述了一名不幸冒险的年轻水手的经历。

e.en: The investor lost money after following {misadvice} online.
e.zh: 这名投资者听信网上的错误建议后亏了钱。

e.en: Patients can be harmed by medical {misadvice}.
e.zh: 患者可能会因误导性的医疗意见而受害。

e.en: A consultant may {misadvise} clients if the data is incomplete.
e.zh: 如果数据不完整，顾问可能会给客户错误建议。

e.en: Do not {misadvise} people about legal deadlines.
e.zh: 不要在法律期限问题上误导他人。

misadvised.t: 被错误建议的；不明智的

e.en: She felt {misadvised} by the financial planner.
e.zh: 她觉得自己受到了理财规划师的错误建议。

e.en: The minister made a {misadvised} public remark.
e.zh: 部长发表了一句不明智的公开言论。

e.en: The guide {misadvises} tourists about local transport.
e.zh: 这本指南在当地交通方面误导游客。

e.en: A careless lawyer who {misadvises} clients risks complaints.
e.zh: 粗心的律师若给客户错误建议，就可能遭到投诉。

e.en: The firm was accused of {misadvising} elderly investors.
e.zh: 这家公司被指控误导老年投资者。

e.en: He denied {misadvising} the patient about the treatment.
e.zh: 他否认在治疗问题上给患者错误建议。

e.en: Hunters can {misaim} when visibility is poor.
e.zh: 能见度差时，猎人可能会瞄错。

e.en: The campaign seemed to {misaim} its message at the wrong voters.
e.zh: 这场竞选似乎把信息传达目标定错了选民。

e.en: A {misaimed} shot broke the kitchen window.
e.zh: 一发瞄错的射击打碎了厨房窗户。

e.en: The ad was {misaimed} at people who could not afford the product.
e.zh: 这则广告把目标定错在买不起该产品的人身上。

e.en: The coach blamed poor balance for her {misaiming}.
e.zh: 教练认为她瞄错是因为平衡感不好。

e.en: The charity was {misaiming} its appeal at wealthy tourists.
e.zh: 这个慈善机构把募捐诉求错误地对准了富裕游客。

e.en: A sudden impact can {misalign} the camera lens.
e.zh: 突然的撞击可能会使相机镜头错位。

e.en: Poor incentives can {misalign} workers' goals with the company's needs.
e.zh: 糟糕的激励机制会让员工目标与公司需求不一致。

misalliance.t: 不合适的联姻；错误联盟

e.en: Her family saw the marriage as a disastrous {misalliance}.
e.zh: 她的家人认为这桩婚姻是灾难性的不当联姻。

e.en: The treaty proved to be a costly {misalliance} for both parties.
e.zh: 事实证明，这项条约对双方都是代价高昂的错误联盟。

e.en: The smaller kingdom was {misallied} with a reckless neighbor.
e.zh: 这个较小的王国与一个鲁莽的邻国结错了盟。

e.en: She felt {misallied} to a family that despised her work.
e.zh: 她觉得自己不该与那个轻视她事业的家族联姻。

e.en: History punishes a leader who {misallies} with unstable powers.
e.zh: 历史会惩罚那些与不稳定势力结错盟的领导者。

e.en: In the novel, the heiress {misallies} herself to a cruel husband.
e.zh: 在小说中，这位女继承人不当地嫁给了一个残忍的丈夫。

e.en: A cautious state should not {misally} with every loud supporter.
e.zh: 谨慎的国家不应和每个高调支持者都结成错误联盟。

e.en: The old families feared she would {misally} beneath her rank.
e.zh: 那些老家族担心她会与身份不相称的人不当联姻。

e.en: The minister was accused of {misallying} the country with extremists.
e.zh: 部长被指责让国家与极端分子结成错误联盟。

e.en: Her relatives warned her against {misallying} with a dishonest suitor.
e.zh: 她的亲戚警告她不要与一个不诚实的求婚者不当联姻。

e.en: The article unfairly labeled every feminist a {misandrist}.
e.zh: 那篇文章不公正地把每个女权主义者都称为厌男者。

e.en: He described the character as a bitter {misandrist}, not a serious critic.
e.zh: 他把这个角色描述成愤恨的厌男者，而不是严肃的批评者。

e.en: The debate confused criticism of sexism with {misandry}.
e.zh: 这场辩论把对性别歧视的批评和厌男混为一谈。

e.en: Some readers saw clear {misandry} in the speaker's remarks.
e.zh: 一些读者在发言者的话里看出了明显的仇视男性。

e.en: His {misanthropical} jokes made the dinner guests uneasy.
e.zh: 他那些厌世的笑话让晚宴客人感到不自在。

e.en: The essay takes a cold, {misanthropical} view of modern cities.
e.zh: 这篇文章以冷漠而厌恶人类的眼光看待现代城市。

e.en: She spoke {misanthropically} about crowds and public celebrations.
e.zh: 她以厌世的口吻谈论人群和公众庆典。

e.en: The narrator {misanthropically} dismisses every act of kindness as vanity.
e.zh: 叙述者厌恶人类似的把每个善举都贬为虚荣。

e.en: The old {misanthropist} preferred books to conversation.
e.zh: 这位老厌世者宁愿读书，也不愿与人交谈。

e.en: He plays a comic {misanthropist} who secretly helps his neighbors.
e.zh: 他扮演一个滑稽的厌世者，却暗中帮助邻居。

e.en: Years of betrayal seemed to {misanthropize} the once generous doctor.
e.zh: 多年的背叛似乎让那位曾经慷慨的医生变得厌世。

e.en: The prison system can {misanthropize} even hopeful reformers.
e.zh: 监狱体系甚至会让满怀希望的改革者变得厌恶人类。

e.en: Do not {misapprehend} my silence as agreement.
e.zh: 不要把我的沉默误解为同意。

e.en: Readers may {misapprehend} the irony if they miss the context.
e.zh: 如果读者忽略语境，可能会误会其中的讽刺。

e.en: She {misapprehended} his warning as a threat.
e.zh: 她把他的警告误解成了威胁。

e.en: His theory was widely {misapprehended} by early reviewers.
e.zh: 他的理论曾被早期评论者广泛误会。

e.en: You are {misapprehending} the purpose of the meeting.
e.zh: 你误解了这次会议的目的。

e.en: The critic kept {misapprehending} satire as simple cruelty.
e.zh: 那位评论家一直把讽刺误会成单纯的刻薄。

e.en: He {misapprehends} caution as cowardice.
e.zh: 他把谨慎误解为怯懦。

e.en: The report {misapprehends} the law's basic purpose.
e.zh: 这份报告误会了该法律的基本目的。

e.en: Her {misapprehensive} reply showed she had missed the joke.
e.zh: 她会错意的回答表明她没有听懂那个玩笑。

e.en: The judge corrected the lawyer's {misapprehensive} reading of the clause.
e.zh: 法官纠正了律师对该条款的误解性解读。

e.en: He nodded {misapprehensively}, thinking the offer was final.
e.zh: 他会错意地点了点头，以为这个提议已经定案。

e.en: The passage was read {misapprehensively} as an attack on science.
e.zh: 这段文字被误解地读成了对科学的攻击。

e.en: Please do not {misarrange} the files after I sort them.
e.zh: 我整理好文件后，请不要把它们排错。

e.en: One careless assistant can {misarrange} an entire day's appointments.
e.zh: 一个粗心的助理可能会把整天的预约安排错。

e.en: He kept {misarranging} the names in alphabetical order.
e.zh: 他一直把这些名字的字母顺序排错。

e.en: The clerk was blamed for {misarranging} the delivery schedule.
e.zh: 那名职员因把送货日程安排不当而受到责备。

e.en: The therapist noted a persistent {misarticulation} of the sound r.
e.zh: 治疗师注意到他一直把 r 这个音发错。

e.en: The policy failed partly because of a serious {misarticulation} of its goals.
e.zh: 这项政策失败，部分原因是其目标表达严重不清。

e.en: The museum corrected the {misascription} of the painting to Rembrandt.
e.zh: 博物馆纠正了把这幅画误署为伦勃朗作品的错误。

e.en: A common {misascription} blames poverty on laziness alone.
e.zh: 一种常见的错误归因把贫困单纯归咎于懒惰。

misbecame.t: 不适合；不相称；有失身份的过去式

e.en: His angry speech {misbecame} a judge of his rank.
e.zh: 他那番愤怒的讲话与他这种级别的法官身份不相称。

e.en: Such carelessness {misbecame} the solemn occasion.
e.zh: 这种粗心在如此庄重的场合显得很不得体。

e.en: Cruel jokes {misbecome} a leader in public.
e.zh: 残忍的玩笑在公开场合不适合一位领导者。

e.en: That gaudy coat would {misbecome} the quiet ceremony.
e.zh: 那件花哨外套会与这场安静的仪式很不相称。

e.en: Petty anger {misbecomes} someone in her position.
e.zh: 小肚鸡肠的怒气不适合她这种身份的人。

e.en: The loud music {misbecomes} this place of mourning.
e.zh: 响亮的音乐与这个哀悼场所很不相称。

e.en: The minister made a {misbecoming} remark at dinner.
e.zh: 那位部长在晚餐上说了一句不得体的话。

e.en: Her bright laughter seemed {misbecoming} during the funeral.
e.zh: 在葬礼上，她爽朗的笑声显得不合时宜。

misbegot.t: 非法所生的；卑劣产生的

e.en: The rumor was a {misbegot} child of fear.
e.zh: 这个谣言是恐惧催生出的丑陋产物。

e.en: He cursed his {misbegot} luck after the trial.
e.zh: 审判后，他咒骂自己那倒霉透顶的运气。

e.en: Her {misbelief} about the medicine delayed treatment.
e.zh: 她对这种药的错误信念耽误了治疗。

e.en: The old {misbelief} still shapes local customs.
e.zh: 这种旧有的误信仍在影响当地习俗。

e.en: Many people {misbelieve} that bats are blind.
e.zh: 许多人误以为蝙蝠是瞎的。

e.en: He did not mean to {misbelieve} her story.
e.zh: 他并不是有意错误地相信她的说法。

e.en: A stubborn {misbeliever} rejected all the evidence.
e.zh: 一个固执的误信者拒绝接受所有证据。

e.en: The preacher called every doubter a {misbeliever}.
e.zh: 那位传教士把每个怀疑者都称为信仰错误的人。

e.en: Such boasting would {misbeseem} a modest scholar.
e.zh: 这种吹嘘会有失一位谦逊学者的体统。

e.en: Bright colors may {misbeseem} the memorial hall.
e.zh: 鲜艳的颜色可能不适合这座纪念堂。

e.en: The king chose to {misbestow} honors on flatterers.
e.zh: 国王竟把荣誉错误地授予阿谀奉承者。

e.en: Do not {misbestow} your trust on strangers.
e.zh: 不要把信任错付给陌生人。

e.en: The villagers feared the calf's {misbirth}.
e.zh: 村民们害怕那头小牛的异常出生。

e.en: The policy was called a {misbirth} of panic.
e.zh: 这项政策被称为恐慌催生的畸形产物。

misbound.t: 装订错误的；误受约束的

e.en: The library returned the {misbound} volume to the printer.
e.zh: 图书馆把那本装订错误的书退给了印刷厂。

e.en: He felt {misbound} by a promise made in fear.
e.zh: 他觉得自己被一个出于恐惧作出的承诺错误地束缚住了。

e.en: Officials said the company would {misbrand} cheap oil as premium.
e.zh: 官员说这家公司会把廉价油错误标称为高端油。

e.en: Do not {misbrand} criticism as hatred.
e.zh: 不要把批评错误地贴上仇恨的标签。

misbranded.t: 贴错标签的；标称不实的

e.en: The store recalled the {misbranded} medicine immediately.
e.zh: 商店立即召回了标签不实的药品。

e.en: She felt {misbranded} as lazy by her manager.
e.zh: 她觉得经理把她错误地说成懒惰。

e.en: A small {miscalibration} caused the sensor to fail.
e.zh: 一次小小的校准错误导致传感器失灵。

e.en: The forecast suffered from political {miscalibration}.
e.zh: 这项预测受到了政治判断失准的影响。

e.en: People often {miscall} this plant a weed.
e.zh: 人们常把这种植物误称为杂草。

e.en: To {miscall} caution cowardice is unfair.
e.zh: 把谨慎误称为懦弱是不公平的。

e.en: The actor was {miscalled} a comedian for years.
e.zh: 多年来那位演员一直被误称为喜剧演员。

e.en: This so-called reform is badly {miscalled}.
e.zh: 这项所谓改革的名称取得很不恰当。

e.en: The teacher apologized for {miscalling} the student.
e.zh: 老师为叫错那名学生的名字道了歉。

e.en: They accused him of {miscalling} propaganda as news.
e.zh: 他们指责他把宣传误称为新闻。

e.en: She often {miscalls} the twins by each other's names.
e.zh: 她常把这对双胞胎的名字互相叫错。

e.en: The report {miscalls} routine delays a crisis.
e.zh: 这份报告把常规延误误称为危机。

e.en: The farmer planted {miscanthus} for biofuel production.
e.zh: 农民种植芒草用于生产生物燃料。

e.en: Tall {miscanthus} swayed beside the winter path.
e.zh: 高高的芒草在冬日小路旁摇曳。

e.en: The archive found several {miscatalogued} letters.
e.zh: 档案馆发现了几封编目错误的信件。

e.en: A {miscatalogued} sample led researchers to the wrong conclusion.
e.zh: 一个归类错误的样本让研究人员得出了错误结论。

e.en: The historian studied {miscegenational} laws in the old colony.
e.zh: 历史学家研究了旧殖民地中与异族通婚有关的法律。

e.en: The novel reflects {miscegenational} anxieties of that era.
e.zh: 这部小说反映了那个时代对异族通婚的焦虑。

e.en: The activist was labeled a {miscegenationist} by hostile newspapers.
e.zh: 敌对报纸把那名活动家称为支持异族通婚的人。

e.en: A quiet {miscegenationist} defended mixed marriages in court.
e.zh: 一位低调的异族通婚支持者在法庭上为混合婚姻辩护。

e.en: The appendix contained {miscella} from earlier drafts.
e.zh: 附录里收有早期草稿中的杂项内容。

e.en: She sorted the {miscella} into labeled folders.
e.zh: 她把这些零散杂物分门别类放进贴好标签的文件夹。

e.en: The drawer was full of {miscellanea} from old trips.
e.zh: 抽屉里满是旧旅行留下的各类杂物。

e.en: The book ends with literary {miscellanea} and notes.
e.zh: 这本书最后附有文学杂录和注释。

e.en: The collection's {miscellaneity} made it hard to catalogue.
e.zh: 这批藏品过于杂乱，编目很困难。

e.en: He enjoyed the cheerful {miscellaneity} of the market.
e.zh: 他喜欢市场里那种热闹而混杂的气息。

e.en: The old {miscellanist} wrote about science, gossip, and travel.
e.zh: 那位老杂文作者写科学、闲谈和旅行。

e.en: A careful {miscellanist} preserved many minor poems.
e.zh: 一位细心的杂集编者保存了许多小诗。

e.en: It was a {mischanceful} voyage from the start.
e.zh: 那次航行从一开始就多灾多难。

e.en: Her {mischanceful} timing cost the team dearly.
e.zh: 她不巧的时机让团队付出了很大代价。

e.en: The teacher knew which {mischief-maker} had hidden the chalk.
e.zh: 老师知道是哪个捣蛋鬼把粉笔藏了起来。

e.en: Online rumors often begin with one determined {mischief-maker}.
e.zh: 网上谣言常常源自一个存心惹事的人。

e.en: The {mischief-makers} laughed when the alarm went off.
e.zh: 警报响起时，那些捣蛋的人笑了起来。

e.en: The policy was meant to discourage political {mischief-makers}.
e.zh: 这项政策旨在阻止政治上的惹事者。

e.en: The children were tired of his constant {mischief-making}.
e.zh: 孩子们受够了他没完没了的捣乱。

e.en: The article accused rivals of {mischief-making} before the vote.
e.zh: 文章指责对手在投票前故意制造事端。

e.en: A {mischiefful} smile crossed the boy's face.
e.zh: 男孩脸上掠过一丝淘气的笑容。

e.en: The play has a {mischiefful} spirit beneath its elegance.
e.zh: 这出戏在优雅之下带着恶作剧般的气质。

e.en: The lighter used {mischmetal} to produce bright sparks.
e.zh: 这个打火机使用铈合金来产生明亮火花。

e.en: Engineers tested {mischmetal} in the experimental alloy.
e.zh: 工程师在实验合金中测试了混合稀土金属。

e.en: A small rod of {mischmetall} sat inside the striker.
e.zh: 击火器里装着一小根铈合金棒。

e.en: The supplier listed {mischmetall} among rare-earth products.
e.zh: 供应商把混合稀土金属列在稀土产品中。

e.en: His {mischoice} of words offended the guests.
e.zh: 他用词不当，冒犯了客人。

e.en: The committee's {mischoice} delayed the project for months.
e.zh: 委员会的错误选择让项目拖延了数月。

e.en: Do not {mischoose} a tool for such delicate work.
e.zh: 做这么精细的活不要选错工具。

e.en: Voters may {mischoose} when information is hidden.
e.zh: 信息被隐瞒时，选民可能会作出错误选择。

e.en: He regretted {mischoosing} the cheaper material.
e.zh: 他后悔选错了那种更便宜的材料。

e.en: The report warned against {mischoosing} partners too quickly.
e.zh: 报告警告不要过快选错合作伙伴。

e.en: She {mischose} her route and arrived late.
e.zh: 她选错了路线，所以迟到了。

e.en: The board {mischose} caution over necessary reform.
e.zh: 董事会错误地选择了谨慎，而不是必要的改革。

e.en: A {mischosen} password can expose private data.
e.zh: 选错的密码可能会暴露私人数据。

e.en: The {mischosen} candidate struggled from the first debate.
e.zh: 那位被误选的候选人从第一次辩论起就很吃力。

e.en: The chemist measured the {miscibility} of oil and solvent.
e.zh: 化学家测量了油和溶剂的可混溶性。

e.en: Poor {miscibility} caused layers to form in the sample.
e.zh: 混溶性差导致样品中形成了分层。

e.en: Alcohol and water are fully {miscible} at room temperature.
e.zh: 酒精和水在室温下可以完全互溶。

e.en: The two liquids were not {miscible} without heat.
e.zh: 不加热时，这两种液体不能互溶。

e.en: The system may {misclassify} rare diseases as common infections.
e.zh: 系统可能把罕见病错误归为常见感染。

e.en: Do not {misclassify} temporary workers as independent contractors.
e.zh: 不要把临时工误归类为独立承包人。

e.en: The clerk might {miscode} the payment in the database.
e.zh: 职员可能会在数据库里把付款编码弄错。

e.en: Researchers can {miscode} responses during manual analysis.
e.zh: 研究人员在手工分析时可能会误编码回答。

e.en: The printer can {miscolor} photos when the cartridge is low.
e.zh: 墨盒快用完时，打印机可能把照片颜色打错。

e.en: Old restorers sometimes {miscolor} damaged sections of paintings.
e.zh: 早期修复师有时会把画作受损部分补错颜色。

e.en: The scan may {miscolour} the fabric under harsh light.
e.zh: 在强光下，扫描可能会把布料颜色显示错。

e.en: A careless editor can {miscolour} the historical costume.
e.zh: 粗心的编辑可能会把历史服装配错颜色。

e.en: Teams often {miscommunicate} when deadlines change quickly.
e.zh: 截止日期快速变化时，团队常会沟通失误。

e.en: I did not mean to {miscommunicate} the client's priorities.
e.zh: 我并不是想把客户的优先事项传达错。

e.en: The critic called the theory a {misconstruction} of the evidence.
e.zh: 评论者称这个理论是对证据的错误解读。

e.en: A small {misconstruction} in the sentence changed its meaning.
e.zh: 句子结构上的一个小错误改变了意思。

e.en: The report corrected several {misconstructions} of the law.
e.zh: 报告纠正了几处对法律的误解。

e.en: His drafts contained awkward {misconstructions} that confused readers.
e.zh: 他的草稿里有些别扭的错误结构，让读者困惑。

e.en: The model showed {misconvergence} after the data were scaled badly.
e.zh: 数据缩放不当后，模型出现了错误收敛。

e.en: Political {misconvergence} can hide real differences between groups.
e.zh: 政治上的不当趋同可能掩盖群体间的真实差异。

e.en: Please check the number; I may have {miscopied} it.
e.zh: 请核对一下号码，我可能把它抄错了。

e.en: The archivist found a {miscopy} of the old letter.
e.zh: 档案员发现了一份误抄的旧信。

e.en: The lawyer was accused of giving {miscounsel} to the client.
e.zh: 那名律师被指给客户提供了错误建议。

e.en: Friends may {miscounsel} you when they misunderstand the risk.
e.zh: 朋友误解风险时，可能会给你出错主意。

e.en: I made a {miscount} and ordered too few chairs.
e.zh: 我数错了，所以椅子订少了。

e.en: Election officials agreed to {miscount} the spoiled ballots separately.
e.zh: 选举官员同意把作废选票另行错误计数。

e.en: She {miscounted} the coins in the jar.
e.zh: 她把罐子里的硬币数错了。

e.en: The survey {miscounted} several households as vacant.
e.zh: 调查把几户有人住的房子误算成空户。

e.en: He kept {miscounting} because people moved around the room.
e.zh: 因为人们在房间里走动，他一直数错。

e.en: The audit found that {miscounting} overtime hours had inflated costs.
e.zh: 审计发现误计加班时数抬高了成本。

e.en: The clerk often {miscounts} change during busy hours.
e.zh: 忙的时候，那名店员常常找零钱数错。

e.en: Two {miscounts} delayed the final election result.
e.zh: 两次数票错误推迟了最终选举结果。

e.en: The judge spoke sternly about the defendant's {miscreance}.
e.zh: 法官严厉谈到了被告的不法行为。

e.en: Old poems sometimes use {miscreance} to mean wickedness.
e.zh: 古诗中有时用这个词表示邪恶行为。

e.en: A careless designer can {miscreate} a feature that confuses users.
e.zh: 粗心的设计师可能会做出让用户困惑的功能。

e.en: The myth says the spirit tried to {miscreate} a second world.
e.zh: 神话说那个精灵试图错误地创造第二个世界。

e.en: The {miscreated} tool solved one problem but caused three others.
e.zh: 这个做坏的工具解决了一个问题，却造成了另外三个。

e.en: In the tale, a {miscreated} creature wanders alone.
e.zh: 在故事里，一个被造坏的生物独自游荡。

e.en: Poor planning {miscreates} systems that no team can maintain.
e.zh: 糟糕的规划会造出没有团队能维护的系统。

e.en: The poem says pride {miscreates} the soul.
e.zh: 诗中说骄傲会扭曲人的灵魂。

e.en: They worried about {miscreating} the character in the film version.
e.zh: 他们担心在电影版中把这个角色塑造错。

e.en: The old sermon warned against {miscreating} nature through vanity.
e.zh: 那篇旧布道告诫人们不要因虚荣而扭曲自然。

miscreative.t: 错误创造的；创造失当的

e.en: The critic found the director's choices strangely {miscreative}.
e.zh: 评论家觉得导演的选择怪异且创造失当。

e.en: A {miscreative} impulse can turn invention into damage.
e.zh: 错误的创造冲动可能把发明变成破坏。

e.en: The tailor {miscut} the fabric and had to start again.
e.zh: 裁缝把布料剪坏了，只好重新开始。

e.en: A {miscut} gemstone may lose much of its value.
e.zh: 切割失误的宝石可能会大幅贬值。

e.en: Historians sometimes {misdate} letters when the ink has faded.
e.zh: 墨迹褪色时，历史学家有时会误判信件年代。

e.en: Do not {misdate} the form, or the office may reject it.
e.zh: 不要把表格日期写错，否则办事处可能会拒收。

misdated.t: 标错日期的；误定年代的

e.en: The museum admitted the vase had been {misdated}.
e.zh: 博物馆承认那个花瓶的年代被误判了。

e.en: A {misdated} invoice caused problems for the accountant.
e.zh: 一张日期写错的发票给会计带来了麻烦。

e.en: The database sometimes {misdates} scanned receipts.
e.zh: 数据库有时会把扫描收据的日期标错。

e.en: Several {misdates} in the timeline confused the researchers.
e.zh: 时间线中的几处日期错误让研究人员感到困惑。

e.en: The scholar was accused of {misdating} the manuscript.
e.zh: 那位学者被指误判手稿的年代。

e.en: Careless {misdating} can invalidate a legal notice.
e.zh: 粗心写错日期可能使法律通知失效。

e.en: The dealer made a {misdeal} and collected the cards again.
e.zh: 发牌员发错了牌，又把牌收了回去。

e.en: A serious {misdeal} of the contract damaged trust.
e.zh: 对合同的严重处理不当损害了信任。

e.en: The player complained that the dealer was {misdealing} again.
e.zh: 那名玩家抱怨发牌员又在发错牌。

e.en: The inquiry examined alleged {misdealing} in public funds.
e.zh: 调查审查了公共资金处理不当的指控。

e.en: If a dealer {misdeals}, the hand must be replayed.
e.zh: 如果发牌员发错牌，这一局必须重来。

e.en: The report lists several {misdeals} in the procurement process.
e.zh: 报告列出了采购流程中的几处处理不当。

e.en: He {misdealt} the cards and apologized to the table.
e.zh: 他发错了牌，向牌桌上的人道歉。

e.en: The agency {misdealt} with the complaint for months.
e.zh: 该机构几个月来一直没有妥善处理这项投诉。

e.en: Do not {misdeem} her silence as consent.
e.zh: 不要把她的沉默误认为同意。

e.en: Old critics might {misdeem} bold writing as mere rudeness.
e.zh: 旧派评论家可能把大胆的写作错判为粗鲁。

e.en: The pamphlet can {miseducate} young readers about health.
e.zh: 这本小册子可能在健康问题上误导年轻读者。

e.en: Schools should not {miseducate} children with outdated history.
e.zh: 学校不应以过时的历史知识错误教育孩子。

e.en: The report's {misemphasis} distorted the real cause of the crisis.
e.zh: 报告的错误强调歪曲了危机的真正原因。

e.en: Her {misemphasis} on speed weakened the quality of the work.
e.zh: 她把重点错放在速度上，削弱了工作质量。

e.en: Writers often {misemploy} technical terms in popular articles.
e.zh: 作者在通俗文章中常会误用专业术语。

e.en: The manager {misemployed} skilled staff on routine clerical tasks.
e.zh: 经理把熟练员工不当地安排去做常规文书工作。

e.en: The audit found serious {misemployment} of public funds.
e.zh: 审计发现公共资金存在严重误用。

e.en: His {misemployment} in a minor role wasted his talent.
e.zh: 把他用在次要岗位上是用人不当，浪费了他的才能。

e.en: The novel's {miserablism} made every victory feel temporary.
e.zh: 小说中的悲惨主义让每一次胜利都显得短暂。

e.en: Critics accused the film of fashionable {miserablism}.
e.zh: 评论家指责这部电影带有时髦的消沉倾向。

e.en: They {misesteem} quietness as a lack of ambition.
e.zh: 他们错误地把安静看成缺乏抱负。

e.en: Public opinion may {misesteem} a leader during a crisis.
e.zh: 公众舆论在危机中可能会错误评价一位领导者。

e.en: Analysts {misestimate} demand when they ignore local habits.
e.zh: 分析师忽视当地习惯时会错误估计需求。

e.en: She {misestimated} the time needed for the repair.
e.zh: 她误判了维修所需的时间。

e.en: A small {misestimation} can ruin the budget.
e.zh: 一个小小的错误估计就可能毁掉预算。

e.en: The disaster resulted from a grave {misestimation} of risk.
e.zh: 这场灾难源于对风险的严重误判。

e.en: The theory describes the {misevolution} of a once-useful trait.
e.zh: 该理论描述了一种曾经有用的性状如何异常演变。

e.en: Institutional {misevolution} turned the reform into a burden.
e.zh: 制度的错误演变把改革变成了负担。

e.en: Teachers can {misexplain} a concept by oversimplifying it.
e.zh: 教师过度简化概念时可能会把它讲错。

e.en: The witness seemed to {misexplain} the sequence of events.
e.zh: 证人似乎把事件发生的顺序解释错了。

e.en: The court identified the contractor as the {misfeasor}.
e.zh: 法院认定承包商为违法行为人。

e.en: A public {misfeasor} may face both dismissal and prosecution.
e.zh: 公职渎职者可能同时面临解职和起诉。

e.en: Users complained that the new shortcut was a {misfeature}.
e.zh: 用户抱怨这个新快捷键是个有害特性。

e.en: The device's main {misfeature} is its confusing reset button.
e.zh: 这台设备的主要设计缺陷是令人困惑的重置按钮。

e.en: Please do not {misfile} the tax receipts again.
e.zh: 请不要再把税务收据归错档了。

e.en: Someone {misfiled} the contract under the wrong client name.
e.zh: 有人把合同错放到了错误的客户名下。

e.en: Poor training can {misform} a student's habits.
e.zh: 糟糕的训练会使学生的习惯形成错误。

e.en: The disease may {misform} the bones during childhood.
e.zh: 这种疾病可能在童年时期导致骨骼发育异常。

e.en: The argument rested on a {misformed} assumption.
e.zh: 这个论证建立在一个形成错误的假设上。

e.en: Doctors noticed a {misformed} valve in the infant's heart.
e.zh: 医生发现婴儿心脏里有一个畸形瓣膜。

e.en: Constant praise was {misforming} his sense of responsibility.
e.zh: 持续的赞扬正在扭曲他对责任的理解。

e.en: The cells were {misforming} under the abnormal pressure.
e.zh: 这些细胞在异常压力下正在发生畸变。

misfuel.t: 加错燃料；燃料使用不当

e.en: Drivers who {misfuel} a diesel car should stop immediately.
e.zh: 给柴油车加错燃料的司机应立即停车。

e.en: The crew {misfueled} the generator before the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨前，工作人员给发电机加错了燃料。

e.en: I may {misgather} your meaning from that brief reply.
e.zh: 我可能会从那句简短回答中误解你的意思。

e.en: Readers could {misgather} that the policy was already approved.
e.zh: 读者可能会错误推断该政策已经获批。

e.en: His silence {misgave} her before the meeting began.
e.zh: 会议开始前，他的沉默让她感到不安。

e.en: The old sailor's warning {misgave} the young captain.
e.zh: 老水手的警告使年轻船长心生疑虑。

e.en: The sudden delay may {misgive} investors.
e.zh: 突然的延期可能会使投资者心生疑虑。

e.en: Her heart began to {misgive} her in the dark hallway.
e.zh: 在黑暗的走廊里，她心里开始不安。

e.en: He felt {misgiven} after reading the strange note.
e.zh: 读完那张奇怪的便条后，他感到心生疑虑。

e.en: A {misgiven} conscience kept her awake all night.
e.zh: 不安的良心让她整夜无法入睡。

e.en: The lawyer's hesitation {misgives} the client.
e.zh: 律师的犹豫让客户心生疑虑。

e.en: Something in his tone {misgives} me.
e.zh: 他语气里的某种东西让我感到不安。

e.en: The king lost his {misgotten} treasure in exile.
e.zh: 国王在流亡中失去了不正当获得的财宝。

e.en: She returned the {misgotten} documents to the clerk.
e.zh: 她把误得的文件还给了办事员。

e.en: Corrupt officials can {misgovern} even a wealthy province.
e.zh: 腐败官员即使在富裕省份也会治理不善。

e.en: The empire began to {misgovern} its distant territories.
e.zh: 帝国开始错误统治其遥远领地。

misgoverned.t: 治理不善的；被错误统治的

e.en: The {misgoverned} city struggled to provide clean water.
e.zh: 这座治理不善的城市难以供应清洁用水。

e.en: A {misgoverned} colony often becomes restless.
e.zh: 被错误统治的殖民地往往会动荡不安。

e.en: The council was accused of {misgoverning} the region for years.
e.zh: 委员会被指多年治理该地区不善。

e.en: A company can fail by {misgoverning} its finances.
e.zh: 公司可能因财务管理失当而失败。

misgovernor.t: 治理不善者；失职统治者

e.en: The pamphlet called the king a cruel {misgovernor}.
e.zh: 那本小册子称国王是残酷的失职统治者。

e.en: Voters finally rejected the {misgovernor} at the polls.
e.zh: 选民最终在投票中否决了那个治理不善者。

e.en: The regime {misgoverns} the province and ignores local needs.
e.zh: 该政权治理这个省不善，并忽视当地需求。

e.en: A board that {misgoverns} risk can destroy a bank.
e.zh: 董事会若风险管理失当，可能毁掉一家银行。

e.en: The report blamed official {misguidance} for the confusion.
e.zh: 报告把混乱归咎于官方的错误指导。

e.en: Children need advice, not careless {misguidance}.
e.zh: 孩子需要建议，而不是草率的误导。

e.en: False statistics can {misguide} public debate.
e.zh: 虚假的统计数据会误导公共讨论。

e.en: The old sign may {misguide} drivers at night.
e.zh: 那块旧标志夜间可能给司机错误指引。

e.en: He was remembered as a {misguider}, not a teacher.
e.zh: 人们记得他是误导者，而不是老师。

e.en: The map app became a {misguider} after the road changed.
e.zh: 道路改道后，那个地图应用成了错误引导者。

e.en: The headline {misguides} readers about the real findings.
e.zh: 这个标题误导读者理解真实研究结果。

e.en: Poor lighting {misguides} visitors toward the wrong exit.
e.zh: 昏暗的灯光把访客引向了错误出口。

e.en: The advertisement was {misguiding} and exaggerated the benefits.
e.zh: 这则广告具有误导性，夸大了好处。

e.en: He kept {misguiding} tourists with outdated directions.
e.zh: 他一直用过时的路线误导游客。

e.en: The room was a {mish-mash} of styles and colors.
e.zh: 这个房间的风格和颜色杂乱混在一起。

e.en: His speech became a {mish-mash} of slogans and jokes.
e.zh: 他的演讲成了一堆口号和笑话的大杂烩。

e.en: The essay portrays him as a bitter {mishellene}.
e.zh: 这篇文章把他描绘成一个尖刻的反希腊者。

e.en: A {mishellene} would reject even Greece's artistic legacy.
e.zh: 厌恶希腊者甚至会否定希腊的艺术遗产。

e.en: She {mishit} the ball into the net.
e.zh: 她击球失误，把球打进了网里。

e.en: A single {mishit} cost the golfer the match.
e.zh: 一次击球失误让那名高尔夫球手输掉了比赛。

e.en: He often {mishits} easy shots under pressure.
e.zh: 他在压力下常把简单的球打偏。

e.en: Two early {mishits} shook her confidence.
e.zh: 开局两次击球失误动摇了她的信心。

e.en: He kept {mishitting} the ball during practice.
e.zh: 他训练时一直把球打偏。

e.en: Her problem was {mishitting}, not lack of power.
e.zh: 她的问题是击球失误，而不是力量不足。

e.en: The rabbi quoted the {Mishna} during the lesson.
e.zh: 拉比在课上引用了《密西拿》。

e.en: Students read the {Mishna} alongside later commentaries.
e.zh: 学生们把《密西拿》和后来的注释一起阅读。

e.en: The scholar studies {Mishnaic} Hebrew grammar.
e.zh: 这位学者研究密西拿希伯来语语法。

e.en: The law reflects an older {Mishnaic} tradition.
e.zh: 这条律法反映了较早的密西拿传统。

e.en: The article compares biblical and {Mishnic} language.
e.zh: 这篇文章比较了圣经语言和密西拿语言。

e.en: He cited a {Mishnic} source for the custom.
e.zh: 他引用了一个密西拿来源来解释这个习俗。

e.en: He {mishook} the rope and dropped the bucket.
e.zh: 他把绳子挂错了，桶掉了下去。

e.en: The fisherman {mishook} the line on a branch.
e.zh: 渔夫把鱼线误钩在树枝上。

e.en: She sometimes {mishooks} the clasp in the dark.
e.zh: 她有时在黑暗中把扣子扣错。

e.en: The crane {mishooks} the load if the angle is wrong.
e.zh: 角度不对时，起重机会把货物挂错。

e.en: The {misdelivery} delayed the contract by a week.
e.zh: 这次误送让合同延误了一周。

e.en: Customers can report a parcel {misdelivery} online.
e.zh: 客户可以在线报告包裹投递错误。

e.en: He did not {misdemean} himself at the hearing.
e.zh: 他在听证会上并没有举止失当。

e.en: A knight who {misdemeans} himself loses honor.
e.zh: 行为不端的骑士会失去荣誉。

e.en: The court treated him as a first-time {misdemeanant}.
e.zh: 法院把他视为初犯轻罪者。

e.en: A {misdemeanant} may receive a fine instead of jail time.
e.zh: 轻罪犯可能被罚款而不是坐牢。

e.en: He had {misdemeaned} himself before the elders.
e.zh: 他在长者面前举止失当。

e.en: The report said the officer {misdemeaned} himself on duty.
e.zh: 报告称那名警官值勤时行为不端。

e.en: She was accused of {misdemeaning} herself in public.
e.zh: 她被指在公共场合举止失当。

e.en: The old rule punished servants for {misdemeaning} themselves.
e.zh: 旧规定会惩罚行为不端的仆人。

e.en: Whoever {misdemeans} himself here will be dismissed.
e.zh: 凡在此举止失当者都会被解雇。

e.en: The code says a guard {misdemeans} himself by accepting gifts.
e.zh: 守则规定，警卫收礼就是行为不端。

e.en: The buyer sued over the {misdescription} of the house.
e.zh: 买方因房屋描述不实而起诉。

e.en: A small {misdescription} in the catalog confused bidders.
e.zh: 目录里一个小小的错误描述让竞标者困惑。

e.en: Doctors can {misdiagnose} rare diseases at first.
e.zh: 医生起初可能会误诊罕见病。

e.en: The software may {misdiagnose} the fault if sensors fail.
e.zh: 如果传感器失灵，软件可能会错误诊断故障。

e.en: I meant to call Mark but {misdialed} the number.
e.zh: 我本想打给马克，却拨错了号码。

e.en: Please hang up if you {misdial} emergency services.
e.zh: 如果误拨了急救电话，请挂断。

e.en: She {misdialled} and reached a pharmacy instead.
e.zh: 她拨错了号码，结果打到了一家药店。

e.en: The call was simply {misdialled}, not suspicious.
e.zh: 那通电话只是拨错了，并不可疑。

e.en: He kept {misdialling} because his hands were shaking.
e.zh: 他因为手在发抖，一直拨错号码。

e.en: Repeated {misdialling} can block the office phone line.
e.zh: 反复误拨可能会占住办公室电话线。

e.en: He admitted he {misdid} the task.
e.zh: 他承认自己把任务做错了。

e.en: The old chronicle says the steward {misdid} his office.
e.zh: 那本古老编年史说管家履职不当。

e.en: The audit found {misdistribution} of relief funds.
e.zh: 审计发现救济资金分配不当。

e.en: A {misdistribution} of heat caused cracks in the glass.
e.zh: 热量分布不均导致玻璃开裂。

e.en: To {misdo} in office was a serious charge.
e.zh: 任职期间行为不端是一项严重指控。

e.en: Beginners often {misdo} the final step.
e.zh: 初学者常常把最后一步做错。

e.en: The {misdoer} apologized to the whole village.
e.zh: 那个做错事的人向全村道歉。

e.en: Old laws often punished the {misdoer} publicly.
e.zh: 旧法律常常公开惩罚作恶者。

e.en: Anyone who {misdoes} the ritual must begin again.
e.zh: 凡是把仪式做错的人都必须重新开始。

e.en: The text says a judge {misdoes} by taking bribes.
e.zh: 文中说法官受贿就是行为不端。

e.en: He denied any {misdoing} in the accounts.
e.zh: 他否认账目中有任何不当行为。

e.en: The apprentice feared {misdoing} the delicate repair.
e.zh: 学徒担心把这项精细修理做错。

e.en: The work was {misdone} and had to be repeated.
e.zh: 这项工作做错了，必须重做。

e.en: He confessed that he had {misdone} against his master.
e.zh: 他承认自己对主人有失当行为。

e.en: Do not {misdoubt} her loyalty without evidence.
e.zh: 没有证据就不要误疑她的忠诚。

e.en: His {misdoubt} grew after the missing letter.
e.zh: 那封信不见后，他的不当怀疑加深了。

e.en: She gave him a {misdoubtful} look.
e.zh: 她用带着误疑的眼神看了他一眼。

e.en: The prince remained {misdoubtful} of honest advice.
e.zh: 王子对诚恳的建议仍抱着不当怀疑。

e.en: He {misdoubts} every promise she makes.
e.zh: 她每作出一个承诺，他都误加怀疑。

e.en: Old {misdoubts} returned when the witness hesitated.
e.zh: 证人犹豫时，旧有的不当怀疑又回来了。

e.en: The parties reached a {mise} before trial.
e.zh: 双方在审判前达成了法律和解。

e.en: The medieval record set out the {mise} clearly.
e.zh: 那份中世纪记录清楚列明了诉讼议题。

e.en: The film's {mise-en-scene} feels cold and precise.
e.zh: 这部电影的场面调度显得冷峻而精确。

e.en: Lighting is central to the stage {mise-en-scene}.
e.zh: 灯光是舞台布景与调度的核心。

e.en: The long voyage filled him with {misease}.
e.zh: 漫长的航程让他满心不适。

e.en: In the poem, winter brings hunger and {misease}.
e.zh: 在诗中，冬天带来饥饿和困苦。

e.en: He lay {miseased} after the rough crossing.
e.zh: 颠簸的渡海之后，他不适地躺着。

e.en: The villagers were {miseased} by famine and cold.
e.zh: 村民们受饥荒和寒冷折磨，困苦不堪。

misinformant.t: 误传消息的人；提供错误情报者

e.en: The reporter relied on a {misinformant} who had misunderstood the event.
e.zh: 记者依赖了一名误传消息的人，而那人误解了事件。

e.en: A careless {misinformant} can damage an entire investigation.
e.zh: 一个粗心的错误情报提供者会破坏整场调查。

misjoinder.t: 不当合并诉讼主体或请求

e.en: The judge dismissed the claim because of {misjoinder} of parties.
e.zh: 法官因当事人不当合并而驳回了该请求。

e.en: The lawyer corrected the {misjoinder} before the trial began.
e.zh: 律师在审判开始前纠正了诉讼请求的不当合并。

e.en: I had to retype the password after a {miskey}.
e.zh: 我误按了一个键，只好重新输入密码。

e.en: The data clerk may {miskey} a number during a long shift.
e.zh: 数据录入员在长时间轮班中可能会输错一个数字。

e.en: His {miskick} sent the ball over the goal.
e.zh: 他一脚踢偏，把球踢过了球门。

e.en: A nervous player may {miskick} under heavy pressure.
e.zh: 紧张的球员在巨大压力下可能会误踢。

e.en: She {miskicked} the ball and lost possession.
e.zh: 她把球踢偏了，结果失去了控球权。

e.en: He {miskicked} the door instead of the box.
e.zh: 他本想踢箱子，却误踢到了门。

e.en: People often {misknow} the causes of old diseases.
e.zh: 人们常常错误理解旧病的成因。

e.en: To {misknow} someone is sometimes worse than not knowing them.
e.zh: 误解一个人有时比不了解他更糟。

e.en: His confidence rested on {misknowledge}, not careful study.
e.zh: 他的自信建立在错误认识上，而不是认真研究。

e.en: The essay explores {misknowledge} as a social problem.
e.zh: 这篇文章把错误认识作为一种社会问题来探讨。

e.en: The store had to recall boxes that workers had {mislabel}ed.
e.zh: 商店不得不召回工人贴错标签的盒子。

e.en: Critics often {mislabel} quiet people as unfriendly.
e.zh: 批评者常把安静的人错误归类为不友善。

e.en: The pilot managed not to {misland} in the strong wind.
e.zh: 飞行员设法没有在强风中错误着陆。

e.en: A tired gymnast can {misland} after a difficult jump.
e.zh: 疲惫的体操运动员在高难度跳跃后可能落地失误。

e.en: Some readers {mislike} the novel's bitter ending.
e.zh: 有些读者不喜欢这部小说苦涩的结尾。

e.en: I do not {mislike} him, though I distrust his plan.
e.zh: 我并不讨厌他，只是不信任他的计划。

e.en: The proposal was {misliked} by nearly everyone in the room.
e.zh: 房间里几乎所有人都不喜欢这个提议。

e.en: He felt unfairly {misliked} by his neighbors.
e.zh: 他觉得邻居们不公平地讨厌他。

misliker.t: 厌恶者；不喜欢某事的人

e.en: A habitual {misliker} of change opposed the new schedule.
e.zh: 一个一贯不喜欢变化的人反对新的时间表。

e.en: The critic was known as a stern {misliker} of sentimental plays.
e.zh: 这位评论家以严厉厌恶感伤戏剧而闻名。

e.en: Her {misliking} of crowds kept her away from festivals.
e.zh: 她不喜欢人群，所以避开了节日活动。

e.en: He was {misliking} the plan more with every delay.
e.zh: 每拖延一次，他就更不喜欢这个计划。

e.en: The printer may {misline} the columns if the paper slips.
e.zh: 如果纸张滑动，打印机可能会把各列排错行。

e.en: Please do not {misline} the page while marking corrections.
e.zh: 标改时请不要在页面上画错线。

mismarriage.t: 不幸婚姻；不合适的结合

e.en: The novel portrays a bitter {mismarriage} between two proud people.
e.zh: 小说描写了两个骄傲的人之间一段痛苦的不幸婚姻。

e.en: The merger became a {mismarriage} of incompatible companies.
e.zh: 这次合并成了两家不相容公司的错误结合。

e.en: Do not {mismate} these cables with the wrong ports.
e.zh: 不要把这些线缆和错误的端口配错。

e.en: The two shoes were a {mismate} from different pairs.
e.zh: 这两只鞋来自不同双，是不相配的一对。

e.en: The machine failed because two parts were {mismated}.
e.zh: 机器出故障是因为两个部件配错了。

e.en: They seemed {mismated} from the first week of marriage.
e.zh: 从婚后第一周起，他们就显得不般配。

e.en: Careless {mismating} of connectors can damage the device.
e.zh: 粗心地配错接头可能会损坏设备。

e.en: The breeder avoided {mismating} animals with known health problems.
e.zh: 饲养者避免把有已知健康问题的动物不当配对。

mismothering.t: 母亲式照顾不当；过度或错误呵护

e.en: The therapist described her control as {mismothering}, not care.
e.zh: 治疗师把她的控制称为错误的母亲式照顾，而不是关爱。

e.en: His {mismothering} made the child anxious rather than secure.
e.zh: 他过度而不当的呵护让孩子焦虑，而不是安心。

e.en: The old philosopher was a declared {misogamist}.
e.zh: 那位老哲学家公开表示自己厌恶婚姻。

e.en: A {misogamist} may still value friendship and family ties.
e.zh: 厌恶婚姻者仍然可能重视友谊和家庭关系。

e.en: The article criticized the film's {misogynic} humor.
e.zh: 文章批评了这部电影中厌女的幽默。

e.en: He denied that his remarks were {misogynic}.
e.zh: 他否认自己的言论带有歧视女性的意味。

e.en: Plato warned against {misology} after bitter arguments.
e.zh: 柏拉图警告人们不要在激烈争论后厌恶理性。

e.en: Public debate suffers when {misology} replaces careful reasoning.
e.zh: 当厌恶论辩取代细致推理时，公共讨论就会受损。

e.en: His {misoneism} made every reform sound dangerous.
e.zh: 他的守旧心理让每项改革听起来都很危险。

e.en: The committee's {misoneism} slowed the adoption of new tools.
e.zh: 委员会对新事物的排斥拖慢了新工具的采用。

misoneist.t: 厌恶新事物的人；守旧者

e.en: A confirmed {misoneist} rejected the online booking system.
e.zh: 这位顽固守旧者拒绝使用网上预订系统。

e.en: She is no {misoneist}; she simply wants evidence first.
e.zh: 她并不是厌恶新事物的人，只是想先看到证据。

e.en: The outage was caused by {misoperation} of the cooling system.
e.zh: 这次停机是冷却系统操作失误造成的。

e.en: Repeated {misoperation} damaged the old printing machine.
e.zh: 反复运转不当损坏了那台旧印刷机。

e.en: Her {misophobia} made crowded trains extremely stressful.
e.zh: 她的洁癖让拥挤的火车变得格外难熬。

e.en: The therapist treated his {misophobia} with gradual exposure.
e.zh: 治疗师通过逐步暴露来治疗他的怕脏恐惧。

e.en: A single {misorder} delayed the restaurant's dinner service.
e.zh: 一份点单错误耽误了餐厅的晚餐服务。

e.en: The clerk managed to {misorder} the pages before binding them.
e.zh: 装订前，职员竟把这些页面排错了顺序。

e.en: The archive was left in a {misorderly} state after the move.
e.zh: 搬迁后，档案被弄得顺序混乱。

e.en: A {misorderly} list can hide important missing records.
e.zh: 顺序错误的清单可能掩盖重要记录的缺失。

e.en: Fog can {misorient} even experienced hikers.
e.zh: 浓雾甚至会让有经验的徒步者迷失方向。

e.en: A faulty compass may {misorient} the survey team.
e.zh: 有故障的指南针可能会误导测量队定位。

e.en: The patient's {misorientation} worsened after midnight.
e.zh: 午夜后，病人的方向感错乱加重了。

e.en: Map errors caused serious {misorientation} among the drivers.
e.zh: 地图错误让司机们严重迷失方向。

misoriented.t: 迷失方向的；定位错误的

e.en: The {misoriented} tourists walked away from the station.
e.zh: 迷失方向的游客离车站越走越远。

e.en: A {misoriented} sensor sent the robot into the wall.
e.zh: 一个定位错误的传感器让机器人撞上了墙。

e.en: The study found a {mispairing} in several DNA samples.
e.zh: 研究在几个DNA样本中发现了错配。

e.en: One {mispairing} of names and photos embarrassed the editor.
e.zh: 一次姓名和照片配错让编辑很尴尬。

e.en: Police opened a {misper} file after the teenager vanished.
e.zh: 那名少年失踪后，警方建立了失踪人员档案。

e.en: The call handler recorded the case as a possible {misper}.
e.zh: 接线员把此案记录为可能的失踪人员案件。

e.en: The miner identified the shiny ore as {mispickel}.
e.zh: 矿工认出那块发亮的矿石是毒砂。

e.en: Old reports warned that {mispickel} could release arsenic fumes.
e.zh: 旧报告警告说，砷黄铁矿可能释放含砷烟气。

e.en: One {misplay} cost the team a certain victory.
e.zh: 一次比赛失误让球队丢掉了稳胜的机会。

e.en: She made a rare {misplay} with the queen of hearts.
e.zh: 她少见地把红桃皇后打错了。

e.en: The midfielder {misplayed} the pass under pressure.
e.zh: 中场球员在压力下把传球处理失误了。

e.en: A {misplayed} card changed the whole bridge hand.
e.zh: 一张打错的牌改变了整副桥牌的局面。

e.en: He kept {misplaying} easy shots near the net.
e.zh: 他不断在网前把简单球打失误。

e.en: {Misplaying} that ace gave her opponent the contract.
e.zh: 打错那张A让她的对手完成了定约。

e.en: The coach counted three {misplays} in the final minute.
e.zh: 教练数出最后一分钟里有三次比赛失误。

e.en: He often {misplays} strong hands by bidding too high.
e.zh: 他常因叫牌过高而把好牌打坏。

e.en: The lawyer warned that they must not {misplead} the claim.
e.zh: 律师警告说，他们不能把诉求陈述错误。

e.en: To {misplead} a defense can weaken the entire case.
e.zh: 抗辩陈述错误可能削弱整个案件。

e.en: The judge allowed an amendment after the {mispleading}.
e.zh: 诉状陈述错误后，法官准许修改。

e.en: Careful drafting reduces the risk of {mispleading}.
e.zh: 仔细起草能降低误辩的风险。

e.en: Do not {misplug} the cable into the audio port.
e.zh: 不要把这根线误插到音频接口里。

e.en: A simple {misplug} left the monitor without power.
e.zh: 一个简单的插错插头让显示器没了电。

e.en: The store had to honor the {mispriced} laptop.
e.zh: 商店不得不按标错的价格出售那台笔记本电脑。

e.en: Analysts argued that the market continued to {misprice} risk.
e.zh: 分析师认为市场仍在错误定价风险。

e.en: Do not {misprise} her silence as agreement.
e.zh: 不要把她的沉默误解为同意。

e.en: He seemed to {misprise} the value of practical experience.
e.zh: 他似乎轻视了实践经验的价值。

e.en: The charge was {misprision} of felony, not the felony itself.
e.zh: 指控是隐匿重罪，而不是重罪本身。

e.en: Old legal texts use {misprision} for certain official misconduct.
e.zh: 旧法律文本用misprision指某些官员渎职行为。

e.en: Critics often {misprize} the patience needed for teaching.
e.zh: 批评者常常低估教学所需的耐心。

e.en: To {misprize} small savings is to miss their long effect.
e.zh: 轻视小额节省，就是忽略它们的长期作用。

e.en: The {misproud} noble refused to speak with merchants.
e.zh: 那位傲慢自负的贵族拒绝与商人交谈。

e.en: His {misproud} answer made the apology sound false.
e.zh: 他骄矜的回答让道歉听起来很不真诚。

e.en: Please do not {mispunctuate} the quoted sentence.
e.zh: 请不要把这句引文的标点标错。

e.en: Students often {mispunctuate} dialogue in early drafts.
e.zh: 学生在初稿中常常把对话的标点用错。

mispunctuated.t: 标点错误的；被误加标点的

e.en: The editor corrected the {mispunctuated} paragraph.
e.zh: 编辑改正了那段标点错误的文字。

e.en: A {mispunctuated} title can change the meaning.
e.zh: 标题标点用错可能会改变意思。

e.en: The article contained a serious {misquotation} of her speech.
e.zh: 那篇文章严重误引了她的讲话。

e.en: He apologized for the {misquotation} in his review.
e.zh: 他为评论中的错误引用道了歉。

e.en: If you {misreckon} the cost, the project may fail.
e.zh: 如果你算错成本，项目可能会失败。

e.en: The sailors {misreckon} the distance in the fog.
e.zh: 水手们在雾中把距离估计错了。

e.en: Their {misreckoning} of demand left shelves empty.
e.zh: 他们对需求估计错误，导致货架空了。

e.en: One small {misreckoning} delayed the whole journey.
e.zh: 一个小小的误算耽误了整段旅程。

e.en: The machine may {misregister} votes if it is damaged.
e.zh: 机器若受损，可能会错误记录选票。

e.en: Old sensors can {misregister} the actual temperature.
e.zh: 旧传感器可能无法正确记录真实温度。

e.en: Hormone {misregulation} can affect sleep and appetite.
e.zh: 激素调节失常会影响睡眠和食欲。

e.en: The report blamed {misregulation} for the market failure.
e.zh: 报告把市场失灵归咎于监管不当。

misrepresentative.t: 不具代表性的；误导性的

e.en: That tiny survey was {misrepresentative} of public opinion.
e.zh: 那项小规模调查并不代表公众意见。

e.en: The chart gives a {misrepresentative} picture of growth.
e.zh: 这张图给出了误导性的增长印象。

e.en: A {misrun} campaign wasted most of the budget.
e.zh: 一场管理不善的活动浪费了大部分预算。

e.en: They feared the system would {misrun} under pressure.
e.zh: 他们担心系统在压力下会运行失当。

missable.t: 容易错过的；可以漏掉的

e.en: The sign is small and easily {missable}.
e.zh: 那个标志很小，很容易被错过。

e.en: Most optional scenes are {missable} on a first playthrough.
e.zh: 第一次游玩时，大多数可选场景都可能漏掉。

e.en: The host corrected the {missaid} name immediately.
e.zh: 主持人立刻纠正了说错的名字。

e.en: Her point was {missaid}, but the meaning was clear.
e.zh: 她的话说得不太准确，但意思很清楚。

e.en: I did not mean to {missay} your title.
e.zh: 我不是有意把你的头衔说错的。

e.en: In nervous moments, speakers may {missay} simple words.
e.zh: 人在紧张时可能会把简单的词说错。

e.en: His {missaying} of the phrase made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 他把那个短语说错，逗得大家都笑了。

e.en: She feared {missaying} the oath during the ceremony.
e.zh: 她担心在仪式上把誓词说错。

e.en: Drivers can {missdistance} objects at night.
e.zh: 司机夜间可能会误判物体距离。

e.en: A slight {missdistance} ruined the long jump.
e.zh: 一点点距离判断错误毁掉了这次跳远。

e.en: His silence may {misseem} like rudeness.
e.zh: 他的沉默可能显得像是无礼。

e.en: The old phrase can {misseem} strange to modern readers.
e.zh: 这个旧说法在现代读者看来可能显得奇怪。

e.en: A {missel} thrush sang from the bare tree.
e.zh: 一只槲鸫在光秃秃的树上歌唱。

e.en: The botanist noted {missel} growing on the branch.
e.zh: 植物学家注意到树枝上长着一种槲寄生。

e.en: Be careful not to {missend} the confidential email.
e.zh: 小心别把那封机密邮件发错。

e.en: The clerk might {missend} the package to another city.
e.zh: 职员可能会把包裹寄错到另一个城市。

e.en: A {missense} mutation changed one protein building block.
e.zh: 一个错义突变改变了蛋白质的一个组成单位。

e.en: The term was used in a {missense} way by the writer.
e.zh: 作者以错误含义使用了这个术语。

e.en: The {missent} email included private details.
e.zh: 那封发错的邮件包含私人信息。

e.en: A {missent} parcel arrived at our office.
e.zh: 一个寄错的包裹送到了我们办公室。

missetting.t: 设置错误；错误背景设定

e.en: A simple {missetting} caused the alarm to ring.
e.zh: 一个简单的设置错误导致警报响起。

e.en: The novel's historical {missetting} annoyed some readers.
e.zh: 小说错误的历史背景设定惹恼了一些读者。

e.en: Too much heat can {misshape} the plastic frame.
e.zh: 过高的热量会使塑料框变形。

e.en: Poor training may {misshape} a young athlete's style.
e.zh: 不良训练可能会让年轻运动员的动作风格走形。

e.en: The pot came out {misshaped} after firing.
e.zh: 陶罐烧制后变形了。

e.en: He wore shoes that made his feet look {misshaped}.
e.zh: 他穿的鞋让脚看起来有些畸形。

e.en: Repeated pressure was {misshaping} the metal plate.
e.zh: 反复受压正在使金属板变形。

e.en: Fear was {misshaping} their view of the facts.
e.zh: 恐惧正在扭曲他们对事实的看法。

e.en: The {missileman} checked the launch controls twice.
e.zh: 那名导弹操作员两次检查了发射控制装置。

e.en: He trained as a {missileman} during his military service.
e.zh: 他服役期间受训成为导弹兵。

e.en: The base stored advanced {missilery} underground.
e.zh: 基地把先进导弹装备储存在地下。

e.en: Modern {missilery} changed military planning completely.
e.zh: 现代导弹技术彻底改变了军事规划。

missilry.t: 导弹技术或导弹装备；疑似拼写变体

e.en: The report discussed {missilry} in modern warfare.
e.zh: 报告讨论了现代战争中的导弹技术。

e.en: Few civilians understand the details of {missilry}.
e.zh: 很少有平民了解导弹装备的细节。

missionize.t: 使带有使命感；派去传教

e.en: The director tried to {missionize} the whole team.
e.zh: 主管试图让整个团队都带上使命感。

e.en: They hoped to {missionize} the remote settlement.
e.zh: 他们希望去那个偏远定居点传教。

missionizer.t: 赋予使命感的人；传教者

e.en: He became a tireless {missionizer} for the reform.
e.zh: 他成了这项改革不知疲倦的倡导者。

e.en: The village remembered the old {missionizer} kindly.
e.zh: 村里人亲切地记得那位老传教者。

e.en: Ask the {missis} before you move the table.
e.zh: 搬桌子前先问问太太。

e.en: The cook said the {missis} wanted dinner early.
e.zh: 厨师说女主人想早点开饭。

missish.t: 像小姐似的；有些矫饰的

e.en: His {missish} manners annoyed the older sailors.
e.zh: 他那种有些矫饰的举止惹恼了老水手们。

e.en: She disliked the {missish} tone of the letter.
e.zh: 她不喜欢那封信里装腔作势的语气。

e.en: The sign spelled {misson} instead of mission.
e.zh: 牌子上把mission误拼成了misson。

e.en: Their {misson} was to repair the bridge.
e.zh: 他们的任务是修好那座桥。

e.en: Please do not {missort} the medical files.
e.zh: 请不要把医疗档案分错类。

e.en: The machine can {missort} letters with damaged labels.
e.zh: 标签破损时，机器可能会把信件分错类。

e.en: Do not {missout} on this chance to learn.
e.zh: 不要错过这个学习机会。

e.en: The list may {missout} several small villages.
e.zh: 这份名单可能遗漏了几个小村庄。

e.en: The minister admitted he {misspoke} during the interview.
e.zh: 部长承认自己在采访中说错了话。

e.en: I {misspoke} when I gave the date yesterday.
e.zh: 我昨天说日期时讲错了。

e.en: Her {misspoken} comment caused a brief argument.
e.zh: 她那句失言引发了一阵短暂争论。

e.en: The name was {misspoken} by the announcer.
e.zh: 播报员把那个名字念错了。

e.en: The draft used {misstatemant} where misstatement was intended.
e.zh: 草稿里把misstatement误写成了misstatemant。

e.en: A serious {misstatemant} can mislead investors.
e.zh: 严重的错误陈述可能误导投资者。

e.en: The two bottles are easily {mistakable} in poor light.
e.zh: 光线不好时，这两个瓶子很容易被弄混。

e.en: His voice is {mistakable} for his brother's.
e.zh: 他的声音可能被误认为是他哥哥的。

e.en: The labels were too {mistakeable} for safe use.
e.zh: 这些标签太容易混淆，使用起来不安全。

e.en: Her handwriting is {mistakeable} for a child's.
e.zh: 她的笔迹容易被误认为是小孩写的。

e.en: Old songs sometimes mention {mistal} at Christmas.
e.zh: 老歌有时会在圣诞节提到槲寄生。

e.en: The word {mistal} appears in a regional glossary.
e.zh: mistal这个词出现在一本地区词汇表里。

e.en: Many students were {mistaught} the old rule.
e.zh: 许多学生被错误地教了那条旧规则。

e.en: She realized her coach had {mistaught} the technique.
e.zh: 她意识到教练把这个技巧教错了。

e.en: A pale {mistbow} formed above the waterfall.
e.zh: 瀑布上方出现了一道淡淡的雾虹。

e.en: The hikers photographed a {mistbow} in the valley.
e.zh: 徒步者拍下了山谷中的雾虹。

e.en: A careless tutor can {misteach} basic grammar.
e.zh: 粗心的家教可能把基础语法教错。

e.en: The book may {misteach} beginners about pronunciation.
e.zh: 这本书可能在发音上误导初学者。

e.en: The inspector found evidence of {misteaching} in the class.
e.zh: 督学发现课堂上有错误教学的迹象。

e.en: Years of {misteaching} left the children confused.
e.zh: 多年的误教让孩子们感到困惑。

e.en: The score marks this passage {misterioso}.
e.zh: 乐谱把这一段标为神秘地演奏。

e.en: A {misterioso} mood filled the opening bars.
e.zh: 开头几小节充满了神秘的气氛。

e.en: The child wrote {mistery} instead of mystery.
e.zh: 那个孩子把mystery误写成了mistery。

e.en: The old house held a strange {mistery}.
e.zh: 那座老房子藏着一件奇怪的神秘事。

e.en: The letter used {mistess} where mistress was meant.
e.zh: 信里把mistress误写成了mistess。

e.en: A careless scribe wrote {mistess} in the margin.
e.zh: 粗心的抄写员在页边写下了mistess这个误拼。

mistflower.t: 雾花；一种开淡紫花的植物

e.en: Blue {mistflower} grows beside the wet path.
e.zh: 蓝色雾花长在潮湿小路旁。

e.en: The gardener planted {mistflower} for autumn color.
e.zh: 园丁种了雾花来增添秋天的色彩。

e.en: A {mistful} dawn softened the whole harbor.
e.zh: 雾气弥漫的黎明让整个港口显得柔和。

e.en: She remembered the {mistful} hills of home.
e.zh: 她想起了家乡那些多雾的山丘。

e.en: We should not {misthink} the problem as simple.
e.zh: 我们不应误以为这个问题很简单。

e.en: People often {misthink} risk when they are afraid.
e.zh: 人在害怕时常常会错误判断风险。

e.en: I had {misthought} the answer at first.
e.zh: 我一开始把答案想错了。

e.en: His {misthought} plan failed immediately.
e.zh: 他那个想错了的计划马上失败了。

e.en: The old poem had a {mistic} tone.
e.zh: 那首古诗带着一种神秘的调子。

e.en: She gave a {mistic} answer to the question.
e.zh: 她对这个问题给出了朦胧难解的回答。

e.en: This was the {mistiest} morning of winter.
e.zh: 这是冬天雾最浓的一个早晨。

e.en: The {mistiest} part of her story came last.
e.zh: 她故事中最模糊的部分出现在最后。

e.en: They played {mistigris} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后他们玩了一种叫mistigris的纸牌游戏。

e.en: The rules of {mistigris} confused the guests.
e.zh: mistigris这种纸牌游戏的规则让客人们很困惑。

e.en: The {mistiness} hid the far hills.
e.zh: 雾气遮住了远处的山丘。

e.en: There was a {mistiness} in his explanation.
e.zh: 他的解释里有一种朦胧不清的感觉。

e.en: The editor may {mistitle} the article.
e.zh: 编辑可能会给这篇文章起错标题。

e.en: Please do not {mistitle} her as director.
e.zh: 请不要误把她称作主任。

e.en: A sprig of {mistle} hung above the door.
e.zh: 门上方挂着一小枝槲寄生。

e.en: The {mistle} sang from the bare tree.
e.zh: 那只画眉鸟在光秃的树上歌唱。

e.en: A {mistlike} veil covered the lake.
e.zh: 湖面笼着一层雾一般的薄纱。

e.en: Her {mistlike} memories returned slowly.
e.zh: 她那些朦胧的记忆慢慢回来了。

e.en: The story was {mistold} for years.
e.zh: 这个故事多年来一直被讲错。

e.en: I was {mistold} about the meeting time.
e.zh: 有人把会议时间错误地告诉了我。

e.en: The letter addressed him as {mistor} Grey.
e.zh: 信里用古称“mistor”称呼格雷先生。

e.en: In the old play, {mistor} meant sir.
e.zh: 在那部旧戏里，mistor的意思是先生。

e.en: The greenhouse used a {mistorizer} for humidity.
e.zh: 温室用喷雾器来保持湿度。

e.en: A broken {mistorizer} soaked the counter.
e.zh: 坏掉的喷雾装置把柜台弄湿了。

e.en: Do not {mistranslate} this legal term.
e.zh: 不要把这个法律术语翻译错。

e.en: Machines can {mistranslate} jokes quite badly.
e.zh: 机器有时会把笑话误译得很离谱。

e.en: The sentence was {mistranslated} in the report.
e.zh: 报告里这个句子被误译了。

e.en: A {mistranslated} label caused confusion.
e.zh: 一个翻译错了的标签造成了混乱。

e.en: The software often {mistranslates} idioms.
e.zh: 这款软件常常把习语翻译错。

e.en: He {mistranslates} simple phrases under pressure.
e.zh: 他一紧张就会把简单短语误译。

e.en: She was {mistranslating} the speaker's joke.
e.zh: 她正在把发言人的笑话翻译错。

e.en: Stop {mistranslating} every technical word literally.
e.zh: 别再把每个技术词都逐字误译了。

e.en: The manuscript spells mistress as {mistres}.
e.zh: 这份手稿把mistress拼作旧式的mistres。

e.en: He called the lady his {mistres}.
e.zh: 他把那位女士称作自己的女主人。

e.en: Her {mistress-ship} of the house was unquestioned.
e.zh: 她作为这所房子的女主人身份无人质疑。

e.en: The scandal concerned his secret {mistress-ship}.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻涉及他秘密的情妇关系。

e.en: The hedge was {mistrimmed} on one side.
e.zh: 树篱有一边被修剪错了。

e.en: A {mistrimmed} hat looked awkward on stage.
e.zh: 一顶装饰不当的帽子在台上显得很别扭。

e.en: He looked at the stranger {mistrustingly}.
e.zh: 他不信任地看着那个陌生人。

e.en: She answered {mistrustingly} after the betrayal.
e.zh: 遭到背叛后，她带着怀疑回答。

mistrustless.t: 没有不信任的；不怀疑的

e.en: His {mistrustless} smile seemed almost naive.
e.zh: 他那毫无疑心的微笑显得近乎天真。

e.en: They wanted a {mistrustless} partnership.
e.zh: 他们想要一种彼此不猜疑的合作关系。

e.en: The technician may {mistune} the old piano.
e.zh: 技师可能会把这架旧钢琴调错音。

e.en: Do not {mistune} the receiver again.
e.zh: 不要再把接收器调得不准了。

e.en: She became {misty-eyed} during the song.
e.zh: 听到那首歌时，她眼里泛起了泪光。

e.en: The speech made everyone {misty-eyed}.
e.zh: 那场演讲让所有人都很感伤。

e.en: I often {mistype} my password.
e.zh: 我经常把密码打错。

e.en: If you {mistype} the address, reload it.
e.zh: 如果你把地址输入错了，就重新加载。

e.en: The guide warns against {misusage} of antibiotics.
e.zh: 指南警告不要误用抗生素。

e.en: This phrase is common despite its {misusage}.
e.zh: 这个短语虽然用法有误，却很常见。

e.en: The judge treated her cooperation as a {mitigator}.
e.zh: 法官把她的合作视为一个减轻因素。

e.en: A calm manager can be a useful {mitigator} during conflict.
e.zh: 在冲突中，冷静的经理可以成为有用的缓和者。

e.en: The lawyer presented {mitigatory} evidence before sentencing.
e.zh: 律师在量刑前提交了减轻责任的证据。

e.en: Her apology had a {mitigatory} effect on the dispute.
e.zh: 她的道歉对这场争端起到了缓和作用。

e.en: The lab tested a {mitoclasic} compound on dividing cells.
e.zh: 实验室在分裂细胞上测试了一种抑制有丝分裂的化合物。

e.en: A {mitoclasic} effect can slow the growth of a tumor sample.
e.zh: 抑制有丝分裂的作用可能减缓肿瘤样本的生长。

e.en: The researchers added a {mitogen} to stimulate cell division.
e.zh: 研究人员加入促有丝分裂原来刺激细胞分裂。

e.en: This protein can act as a {mitogen} in immune cells.
e.zh: 这种蛋白质能在免疫细胞中充当促分裂原。

e.en: The study measured {mitogenesis} after exposure to the drug.
e.zh: 这项研究测量了接触药物后的有丝分裂发生情况。

e.en: Abnormal {mitogenesis} may contribute to uncontrolled tissue growth.
e.zh: 异常的有丝分裂发生可能导致组织失控生长。

e.en: The team examined the {mitogenetic} response of lymphocytes.
e.zh: 团队检查了淋巴细胞的促有丝分裂反应。

e.en: A weak {mitogenetic} signal was detected in the culture.
e.zh: 培养物中检测到微弱的促有丝分裂信号。

e.en: The compound showed strong {mitogenic} activity in the assay.
e.zh: 该化合物在测定中表现出很强的促有丝分裂活性。

e.en: Some growth factors are highly {mitogenic} for skin cells.
e.zh: 一些生长因子对皮肤细胞有很强的促分裂作用。

e.en: The microscope revealed {mitokinetic} changes in the chromosomes.
e.zh: 显微镜显示出染色体的有丝分裂运动变化。

e.en: She focused on {mitokinetic} patterns during early cell division.
e.zh: 她关注早期细胞分裂中的有丝分裂运动模式。

e.en: A {mitoribosome} helps produce proteins inside mitochondria.
e.zh: 线粒体核糖体帮助在线粒体内生成蛋白质。

e.en: The mutation disrupted normal {mitoribosome} assembly.
e.zh: 这种突变破坏了线粒体核糖体的正常组装。

e.en: Under these conditions, the cells {mitose} more rapidly.
e.zh: 在这些条件下，细胞进行有丝分裂的速度更快。

e.en: The tissue seemed to {mitose} after the treatment.
e.zh: 治疗后，这种组织似乎开始进行有丝分裂。

e.en: The antibody was designed to detect {mitosin} in tumor cells.
e.zh: 这种抗体被设计用来检测肿瘤细胞中的有丝分裂素蛋白。

e.en: Levels of {mitosin} rose as the cells prepared to divide.
e.zh: 随着细胞准备分裂，有丝分裂素蛋白的水平升高了。

e.en: Each {mitosporangium} releases spores without sexual reproduction.
e.zh: 每个有丝孢子囊都会释放不经有性繁殖形成的孢子。

e.en: The fungus formed a small {mitosporangium} on the damp wood.
e.zh: 这种真菌在潮湿木头上形成了一个小的有丝孢子囊。

e.en: A {mitospore} can develop without a sexual cycle.
e.zh: 有丝孢子可以不经过有性周期而发育。

e.en: The mold spread quickly by producing {mitospores}.
e.zh: 这种霉菌通过产生有丝孢子迅速扩散。

e.en: The cells divided {mitotically} under the microscope.
e.zh: 这些细胞在显微镜下通过有丝分裂进行分裂。

e.en: This lineage is transmitted {mitotically} from one cell to another.
e.zh: 这一谱系通过有丝分裂从一个细胞传到另一个细胞。

e.en: The museum displayed a French {mitrailleuse} from the 1870s.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一挺十九世纪七十年代的法国早期机关枪。

e.en: Soldiers feared the {mitrailleuse} because it fired many rounds quickly.
e.zh: 士兵害怕这种早期机关枪，因为它能快速发射许多子弹。

e.en: He clamped the trim against a {mitreblock} before cutting.
e.zh: 切割前，他把饰条夹在斜接垫块上。

e.en: A worn {mitreblock} can make the corner joint inaccurate.
e.zh: 磨损的斜接垫块会让角接缝不准确。

e.en: The carpenter used a {mitreboard} to guide the saw.
e.zh: 木匠用斜接板来引导锯子。

e.en: A simple {mitreboard} helps beginners cut cleaner angles.
e.zh: 简单的斜切导板能帮助初学者切出更整齐的角度。

e.en: She cut the frame pieces in a {mitrebox}.
e.zh: 她在斜接盒里切割画框木条。

e.en: A {mitrebox} keeps the saw at a fixed angle.
e.zh: 斜切盒能让锯子保持固定角度。

e.en: The shady bank was covered with {mitrewort} in spring.
e.zh: 春天，阴凉的河岸上长满了主教帽草。

e.en: Botanists identified the tiny white flower as {mitrewort}.
e.zh: 植物学家把这种小白花鉴定为主教帽草。

e.en: The shell had a {mitriform} shape near the tip.
e.zh: 这个贝壳靠近尖端处呈冠帽状。

e.en: A {mitriform} cap covered the young fungal body.
e.zh: 一个冠帽状的菌盖覆盖着幼小的真菌体。

e.en: The rabbi explained the {mitsvah} to the children.
e.zh: 拉比向孩子们解释这条诫命。

e.en: Helping your neighbor is a real {mitsvah}.
e.zh: 帮助邻居确实是一件善行。

e.en: The judge signed the {mittimus} after sentencing.
e.zh: 法官宣判后签署了收监令。

e.en: The clerk prepared a {mittimus} for the prison transfer.
e.zh: 书记员为移送监狱准备了移送令。

e.en: The old grain smelled dusty and {mity}.
e.zh: 那批旧谷物闻起来又 dusty 又像有螨虫。

e.en: A {mity} infestation damaged the stored cheese.
e.zh: 螨虫滋生损坏了储存的奶酪。

e.en: Fold the chocolate chips in as a {mix-in}.
e.zh: 把巧克力豆作为混入配料拌进去。

e.en: The developer added a small {mix-in} for logging.
e.zh: 开发者添加了一个用于记录日志的小型混入组件。

e.en: There was a {mix-up} with our hotel booking.
e.zh: 我们的酒店预订出了差错。

e.en: The similar names caused a serious {mix-up}.
e.zh: 相似的名字造成了严重混淆。

e.en: Several {mix-ups} delayed the delivery.
e.zh: 几次差错耽误了送货。

e.en: Clear labels prevent {mix-ups} in the lab.
e.zh: 清楚的标签能防止实验室里发生混淆。

e.en: The powder is {mixable} with cold water.
e.zh: 这种粉末可以和冷水混合。

e.en: Choose colors that are easily {mixable}.
e.zh: 选择容易调配的颜色。

e.en: The album's {mixage} gives the drums more space.
e.zh: 这张专辑的混音处理让鼓声更有空间感。

e.en: The chef praised the subtle {mixage} of spices.
e.zh: 厨师称赞这些香料搭配得很微妙。

e.en: The novel uses {mixblood} as an outdated term.
e.zh: 这部小说把“混血者”作为一个过时说法来使用。

e.en: He rejected the label {mixblood} in official records.
e.zh: 他拒绝在官方记录中被标为混血身份。

mixed-ability.t: 能力混合的；水平参差的

e.en: She teaches a {mixed-ability} class of teenagers.
e.zh: 她教一个水平参差的青少年班。

e.en: The course includes {mixed-ability} group work.
e.zh: 这门课包含能力混合的小组活动。

e.en: The phrase {mixed-blood} now sounds dated to many people.
e.zh: 许多人现在觉得“混血的”这个说法有些过时。

e.en: He was described as {mixed-blood} in the old census.
e.zh: 在旧人口普查中，他被描述为混血者。

e.en: The simulation used a {mixed-congruential} random number generator.
e.zh: 这次模拟使用了混合同余随机数生成器。

e.en: A {mixed-congruential} method includes an added constant.
e.zh: 混合同余方法包含一个附加常数。

e.en: My notes are completely {mixed-up} after the meeting.
e.zh: 会后我的笔记完全乱了。

e.en: She felt {mixed-up} about what to do next.
e.zh: 她对下一步该做什么感到很迷茫。

e.en: They built a {mixed-use} complex near the station.
e.zh: 他们在车站附近建了一座混合用途综合体。

e.en: The plan encourages {mixed-use} development downtown.
e.zh: 这项规划鼓励市中心进行混合用途开发。

e.en: Old recipes sometimes spell {mixen} where modern writers use mixing.
e.zh: 旧食谱有时写作 mixen，现代作者则用 mixing。

e.en: The dialect word {mixen} appeared in the glossary.
e.zh: 这个方言词 mixen 出现在词汇表中。

mixis.t: 水体混合现象或过程；混合

e.en: Spring winds caused {mixis} throughout the lake.
e.zh: 春风使整片湖水发生了混合。

e.en: The report describes seasonal {mixis} in deep reservoirs.
e.zh: 报告描述了深水水库中的季节性混合现象。

e.en: The party hired a {mixmaster} for the cocktail bar.
e.zh: 派对请了一位调酒高手负责鸡尾酒吧。

e.en: He became the studio's {mixmaster} for complex soundtracks.
e.zh: 他成了录音棚里处理复杂配乐的混音能手。

mixmastered.t: 被熟练混合或调配过的

e.en: The DJ {mixmastered} the tracks into one long set.
e.zh: 那位DJ把这些曲目熟练混成了一整套长节目。

e.en: She {mixmastered} fresh juices for the brunch crowd.
e.zh: 她为早午餐的客人熟练调配新鲜果汁。

mixmastering.t: 熟练混合或调配的过程

e.en: He spent the evening {mixmastering} old funk records.
e.zh: 他整个晚上都在熟练混合老放克唱片。

e.en: The bartender was {mixmastering} drinks behind the counter.
e.zh: 调酒师正在柜台后调配饮品。

e.en: The lab compared each flour sample with a {mixogram}.
e.zh: 实验室用搅拌曲线图比较每份面粉样品。

e.en: A strong gluten flour gives a higher {mixogram} peak.
e.zh: 高筋面粉会在搅拌曲线图上显示更高的峰值。

e.en: Fish gathered in the oxygen-rich {mixolimnion}.
e.zh: 鱼群聚集在富含氧气的湖泊上层混合水层。

e.en: Summer heating made the {mixolimnion} unusually shallow.
e.zh: 夏季升温使湖泊上层混合水层异常变浅。

e.en: The {mixologist} recommended a smoky mezcal cocktail.
e.zh: 调酒师推荐了一款带烟熏味的梅斯卡尔鸡尾酒。

e.en: A good {mixologist} balances sweetness, acid, and aroma.
e.zh: 优秀的鸡尾酒专家会平衡甜味、酸度和香气。

e.en: She studied {mixology} before opening her own bar.
e.zh: 她在开自己的酒吧前学习了调酒术。

e.en: Modern {mixology} often borrows ideas from cooking.
e.zh: 现代鸡尾酒调制常常借鉴烹饪中的想法。

e.en: The melody has a bright {mixolydian} feel.
e.zh: 这段旋律带有明亮的混合利底亚调式感觉。

e.en: Guitarists often use the {mixolydian} mode over dominant chords.
e.zh: 吉他手常在属和弦上使用混合利底亚调式。

e.en: Some algae are {mixotrophic} under low light.
e.zh: 有些藻类在弱光下属于混合营养型。

e.en: The {mixotrophic} organism can both photosynthesize and feed.
e.zh: 这种混合营养型生物既能光合作用，也能摄食。

e.en: Researchers measured {mixotrophy} in coastal plankton communities.
e.zh: 研究人员测量了沿海浮游生物群落中的混合营养方式。

e.en: For some microbes, {mixotrophy} improves survival during shortages.
e.zh: 对某些微生物来说，混合营养有助于在资源短缺时生存。

e.en: The poet wrote of joy {mixt} with grief.
e.zh: 诗人写到喜悦中混杂着悲伤。

e.en: A {mixt} crowd filled the old market square.
e.zh: 一群成分混杂的人挤满了老市场广场。

e.en: The restorer applied {mixtion} before laying the gold leaf.
e.zh: 修复师在贴金箔前涂上了镀金黏合剂。

e.en: Old manuals use {mixtion} to mean a careful mixing.
e.zh: 旧手册里用mixtion表示细致的混合。

e.en: The geologist identified the layer as {mixtite}.
e.zh: 地质学家把这一层鉴定为混合成因沉积岩。

e.en: A {mixtite} may contain fragments from several sources.
e.zh: 混合成因沉积岩可能含有来自多个来源的碎屑。

e.en: There was a {mixup} with our hotel booking.
e.zh: 我们的酒店预订出了点差错。

e.en: The files were lost after a serious {mixup}.
e.zh: 一场严重混乱后，那些文件丢失了。

e.en: The sailor climbed the {mizen} during the drill.
e.zh: 演练时，水手爬上了船的后桅。

e.en: A torn {mizen} sail slowed the old vessel.
e.zh: 破损的后桅帆拖慢了那艘旧船。

e.en: The storm cracked the ship's {mizenmast}.
e.zh: 暴风雨折裂了船上的后桅。

e.en: A small flag flew from the {mizenmast}.
e.zh: 一面小旗从后桅上飘着。

e.en: Children ran through the old turf {mizmaze}.
e.zh: 孩子们跑过那座古老的草地迷宫。

e.en: The legal papers formed a {mizmaze} of conditions.
e.zh: 这些法律文件构成了一团错综复杂的条件迷宫。

e.en: She added fresh {mizuna} to the salad.
e.zh: 她把新鲜水菜加进沙拉里。

e.en: The chef wilted the {mizuna} with garlic.
e.zh: 厨师用蒜把水菜稍微炒软。

e.en: The {mizzen} helped steady the old ship.
e.zh: 后桅帮助那艘旧船保持稳定。

e.en: A tear appeared in the {mizzen} during the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨中后桅帆裂开了一道口子。

e.en: The crew repaired the {mizzenmast} before dawn.
e.zh: 船员们在黎明前修好了后桅。

e.en: A lantern hung from the {mizzenmast}.
e.zh: 一盏灯挂在船尾的后桅上。

e.en: The {mizzensail} caught the evening wind.
e.zh: 后桅帆迎住了傍晚的风。

e.en: They lowered the {mizzensail} as the gale rose.
e.zh: 大风增强时，他们降下了后桅帆。

e.en: A cold {mizzle} covered the fields.
e.zh: 一阵冷冷的细雨笼罩了田野。

e.en: It began to {mizzle} after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后开始下起毛毛雨。

e.en: It {mizzled} all morning by the harbor.
e.zh: 港口边整个上午都下着毛毛雨。

e.en: The {mizzled} road shone under the lamps.
e.zh: 被细雨打湿的道路在灯下发亮。

e.en: It often {mizzles} here in November.
e.zh: 这里十一月常常下毛毛雨。

e.en: Soft {mizzles} blurred the distant hills.
e.zh: 轻柔的细雨模糊了远处的山丘。

e.en: A {mizzling} rain followed us home.
e.zh: 一阵毛毛细雨一路伴着我们回家。

e.en: They walked through the {mizzling} streets.
e.zh: 他们走过正飘着细雨的街道。

e.en: We woke to a {mizzly} morning.
e.zh: 我们醒来时，早晨细雨蒙蒙。

e.en: The match continued in {mizzly} weather.
e.zh: 比赛在细雨蒙蒙的天气里继续进行。

e.en: The philosopher used {mneme} to mean memory itself.
e.zh: 那位哲学家用mneme指记忆本身。

e.en: Each habit leaves a kind of {mneme}.
e.zh: 每个习惯都会留下一种记忆痕迹。

e.en: The study examined {mnemic} traces in the brain.
e.zh: 这项研究考察了大脑中的记忆痕迹。

e.en: She built a {mnemic} pattern from colors.
e.zh: 她用颜色构建了一个助记模式。

e.en: He preferred a {mnemonical} verse for dates.
e.zh: 他更喜欢用助记诗来记日期。

e.en: The teacher gave a {mnemonical} rule.
e.zh: 老师给出了一条助记规则。

e.en: The planets were arranged {mnemonically} in a rhyme.
e.zh: 这些行星被编进押韵句中来帮助记忆。

e.en: She coded the steps {mnemonically}.
e.zh: 她用助记方式给这些步骤编码。

e.en: The {mnemonist} recalled hundreds of numbers.
e.zh: 那位记忆高手记起了数百个数字。

e.en: A trained {mnemonist} uses vivid mental images.
e.zh: 受过训练的记忆术专家会使用鲜明的心理图像。

e.en: The tutor taught a {mnemotechnic} method.
e.zh: 导师教授了一种助记法。

e.en: His {mnemotechnic} notes turned facts into stories.
e.zh: 他的记忆术笔记把事实变成了故事。

e.en: She studied {mnemotechnics} before the contest.
e.zh: 比赛前她学习了记忆术。

e.en: Ancient speakers relied on {mnemotechnics}.
e.zh: 古代演说家依靠助记技巧。

e.en: The {mnemotechnist} trained actors to remember lines.
e.zh: 这位记忆术专家训练演员记台词。

e.en: As a {mnemotechnist}, he designed memory palaces.
e.zh: 作为记忆术专家，他设计了记忆宫殿。

e.en: Archaeologists found evidence of {moa-hunting} camps.
e.zh: 考古学家发现了猎捕恐鸟营地的证据。

e.en: The lecture discussed {moa-hunting} in early New Zealand.
e.zh: 讲座讨论了早期新西兰的猎捕恐鸟活动。

mobsman.t: 暴徒成员；匪帮成员；窃贼团伙成员

e.en: The {mobsman} slipped away before the police arrived.
e.zh: 警察到达前，那个匪帮成员溜走了。

e.en: In old crime stories, a {mobsman} often knew every alley.
e.zh: 在旧式犯罪小说里，匪帮成员常常熟悉每条小巷。

mock-heroic.t: 滑稽模仿英雄体的；假装英勇的

e.en: The poem uses a {mock-heroic} style to describe a quarrel over tea.
e.zh: 这首诗用滑稽模仿英雄体的风格描写一场关于茶的争吵。

e.en: He gave a {mock-heroic} salute before lifting the heavy suitcase.
e.zh: 他在提起那个沉重行李箱前，装模作样地敬了个英雄式的礼。

mock-heroically.t: 以滑稽英雄体；装作英勇地

e.en: She spoke {mock-heroically} about surviving the long meeting.
e.zh: 她用滑稽夸张的英雄口吻谈起自己熬过了那场长会。

e.en: He {mock-heroically} raised the broken umbrella like a sword.
e.zh: 他装作英勇地把坏伞像剑一样举起来。

mock-serious.t: 假装严肃的；一本正经地开玩笑的

e.en: Her {mock-serious} warning made everyone laugh.
e.zh: 她一本正经开玩笑似的警告把大家都逗笑了。

e.en: He wore a {mock-serious} expression while announcing the cake rules.
e.zh: 他宣布吃蛋糕规则时摆出一副假装严肃的表情。

mock-up.t: 模型；实物样稿；界面原型

e.en: The designer showed a {mock-up} of the new app.
e.zh: 设计师展示了新应用的界面原型。

e.en: Engineers built a full-size {mock-up} of the cabin.
e.zh: 工程师做了一个驾驶舱的全尺寸模型。

e.en: The team reviewed three website {mock-ups} before lunch.
e.zh: 团队午饭前审查了三个网站原型图。

e.en: Architects use {mock-ups} to test materials and lighting.
e.zh: 建筑师用实物样稿来测试材料和采光效果。

e.en: His {mockage} of the speech felt cruel rather than funny.
e.zh: 他对那段演讲的嘲弄让人觉得刻薄，而不是好笑。

e.en: The play turns political {mockage} into sharp comedy.
e.zh: 这部戏把政治讥讽变成了犀利的喜剧。

e.en: A {mockbird} sang loudly from the fence at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时，一只嘲鸫在篱笆上高声鸣唱。

e.en: The old name {mockbird} refers to a bird that imitates sounds.
e.zh: mockbird这个旧称指会模仿声音的鸟。

e.en: The young singer ignored the {mockers} in the crowd.
e.zh: 那位年轻歌手没有理会人群中的嘲笑者。

e.en: Online {mockers} quickly turned the mistake into a joke.
e.zh: 网上那些讥讽的人很快把这个错误变成了笑料。

mocket.t: 假货；仿制品；旧式仿造物

e.en: The jeweler warned that the stone was only a {mocket}.
e.zh: 珠宝商提醒说，那块石头只是仿制品。

e.en: In the market, he bought a cheap {mocket} of a famous medal.
e.zh: 他在市场上买了一枚名牌奖章的廉价仿造物。

e.en: A {mockie} copied the ringtone from a nearby porch.
e.zh: 一只嘲鸫模仿了附近门廊传来的手机铃声。

e.en: Locals call the noisy little bird a {mockie}.
e.zh: 当地人把这种吵闹的小鸟叫作mockie。

e.en: A {mocking-bird} repeated the calls of other birds.
e.zh: 一只嘲鸫反复模仿其他鸟的叫声。

e.en: The child watched a {mocking-bird} on the telephone wire.
e.zh: 孩子看着电话线上停着的一只嘲鸫。

mockney.t: 假伦敦东区口音；装工人腔的人

e.en: The actor's {mockney} accent sounded forced to local viewers.
e.zh: 当地观众觉得那名演员假装的伦敦东区口音很做作。

e.en: Critics called him a {mockney} because he came from a wealthy family.
e.zh: 评论者说他装工人腔，因为他出身富裕家庭。

mockumentary.t: 伪纪录片；仿纪录片喜剧

e.en: The series is a {mockumentary} about office life.
e.zh: 这部剧是一部关于办公室生活的伪纪录片。

e.en: A good {mockumentary} can make fake interviews feel real.
e.zh: 优秀的伪纪录片能让虚构采访显得很真实。

e.en: Please send me the final {mockup} before development starts.
e.zh: 开发开始前，请把最终设计原型发给我。

e.en: The museum displayed a {mockup} of the spacecraft interior.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一件航天器内部的模型。

mocky.t: 带嘲弄意味的；爱讥笑的

e.en: His {mocky} tone made the apology sound insincere.
e.zh: 他带嘲弄意味的语气让道歉听起来不真诚。

e.en: She gave him a {mocky} smile after his bold claim.
e.zh: 他夸下海口后，她冲他露出一个讥讽的笑。

mocock.t: 雄性莫卡鸭；旧称野鸭公鸟

e.en: The hunter identified the bird as a {mocock} in his old field notes.
e.zh: 猎人在旧野外笔记中把那只鸟记作雄性莫卡鸭。

e.en: Few modern readers recognize the word {mocock}.
e.zh: 如今很少有读者认得mocock这个词。

modacrylic.t: 改性腈纶；变性丙烯酸纤维

e.en: The wig was made from heat-resistant {modacrylic} fiber.
e.zh: 这顶假发由耐热的改性腈纶纤维制成。

e.en: Manufacturers use {modacrylic} in blankets and protective clothing.
e.zh: 制造商把改性腈纶用于毯子和防护服。

e.en: The doctor prescribed {modafinil} for narcolepsy.
e.zh: 医生开了莫达非尼来治疗发作性睡病。

e.en: Some students misuse {modafinil} to stay awake while studying.
e.zh: 有些学生滥用莫达非尼来熬夜学习。

e.en: Her {moderatism} made her acceptable to both parties.
e.zh: 她的温和主义让两党都能接受她。

e.en: The essay defends political {moderatism} in a polarized age.
e.zh: 这篇文章在两极分化的时代为政治温和主义辩护。

e.en: He ran as a {moderatist} in the local election.
e.zh: 他以温和派人士的身份参加地方选举。

e.en: The {moderatist} wing rejected the harsher proposal.
e.zh: 温和派阵营拒绝了那项更严厉的提案。

e.en: The committee played a {moderative} role in the dispute.
e.zh: 委员会在这场争端中发挥了缓和作用。

e.en: She preferred a {moderative} tone when discussing reform.
e.zh: 谈到改革时，她更喜欢节制的语气。

e.en: The sonata begins {moderato} before turning lively.
e.zh: 这首奏鸣曲以中板开始，随后变得活泼。

e.en: Play this passage {moderato}, not too slowly.
e.zh: 这段要按中板演奏，不要太慢。

e.en: Her {moderatorship} improved the quality of the debate.
e.zh: 她担任主持人后，辩论质量提高了。

e.en: He lost his {moderatorship} after ignoring forum rules.
e.zh: 他因无视论坛规则而失去了版主身份。

e.en: The story is set in {modern-day} London.
e.zh: 这个故事发生在当代伦敦。

e.en: Many {modern-day} workers rely on digital tools.
e.zh: 许多现代工作者依赖数字工具。

e.en: The theater staged a {modern-dress} Hamlet.
e.zh: 剧院上演了一版现代服装的《哈姆雷特》。

e.en: A {modern-dress} production can make old dialogue feel fresh.
e.zh: 现代服装版演出能让古老台词显得新鲜。

e.en: They moved into a {modern-looking} apartment near the station.
e.zh: 他们搬进了车站附近一套看起来很现代的公寓。

e.en: The phone has a {modern-looking} screen and slim frame.
e.zh: 这部手机有现代感的屏幕和纤薄边框。

e.en: Her {modern-minded} parents supported her career choice.
e.zh: 她思想开明的父母支持她的职业选择。

e.en: The school needs a {modern-minded} principal.
e.zh: 这所学校需要一位思想现代的校长。

e.en: The village includes a {modernbuilt} hall beside the church.
e.zh: 村里在教堂旁有一座现代建造的礼堂。

e.en: A {modernbuilt} wing was added to the old museum.
e.zh: 这座老博物馆增建了一翼现代建筑。

e.en: The novel retells the myth in a {modernday} setting.
e.zh: 这部小说把神话放在当代背景中重述。

e.en: He studies {modernday} problems through ancient philosophy.
e.zh: 他用古代哲学研究现代问题。

e.en: The lobby was decorated {modernistically} with glass and steel.
e.zh: 大厅用玻璃和钢材装饰，带有现代主义风格。

e.en: She writes {modernistically}, breaking the usual narrative order.
e.zh: 她以现代主义方式写作，打破通常的叙事顺序。

e.en: A {modernminded} manager welcomed flexible working hours.
e.zh: 一位思想开明的经理接受了弹性工作时间。

e.en: The reforms appealed to {modernminded} voters.
e.zh: 这些改革吸引了思想现代的选民。

e.en: He tried to {modge} the broken chair with tape.
e.zh: 他想用胶带把坏椅子凑合修好。

e.en: The report was {modged} together at the last minute.
e.zh: 那份报告是最后一刻东拼西凑出来的。

e.en: The software's {modifiability} made it useful for researchers.
e.zh: 这款软件的可修改性使它对研究人员很有用。

e.en: Biologists studied the {modifiability} of the organism's behavior.
e.zh: 生物学家研究了这种生物行为的可改变性。

e.en: In this formula, x is the {modificand}.
e.zh: 在这个公式中，x 是被修改项。

e.en: The adjective must agree with its {modificand}.
e.zh: 这个形容词必须与它所修饰的词保持一致。

modificative.t: 修改性的；起修饰作用的

e.en: The clause has a {modificative} function in the sentence.
e.zh: 这个从句在句中起修饰作用。

e.en: The law introduced only {modificative} changes to the system.
e.zh: 这项法律只是对制度作了修改性的调整。

e.en: The editor acted as a careful {modificator} of the draft.
e.zh: 编辑作为细致的修改者处理了草稿。

e.en: In grammar, an adverb can serve as a {modificator}.
e.zh: 在语法中，副词可以充当修饰语。

e.en: The judge issued a {modificatory} order after the appeal.
e.zh: 上诉后，法官发布了一项修改令。

e.en: Some prefixes have a mainly {modificatory} effect.
e.zh: 有些前缀主要起修饰作用。

e.en: A carved {modillion} supported the cornice.
e.zh: 一个雕刻的檐下托臂支撑着檐口。

e.en: The architect restored each {modillion} on the old facade.
e.zh: 建筑师修复了旧立面上的每个飞檐托饰。

e.en: The house had a {modillioned} cornice above the porch.
e.zh: 这栋房子的门廊上方有带檐下托臂装饰的檐口。

e.en: We admired the {modillioned} facade of the courthouse.
e.zh: 我们欣赏了法院大楼那带飞檐托饰的立面。

modioliform.t: 蜗轴状的；螺旋状的管形结构

e.en: The fossil had a {modioliform} inner curve.
e.zh: 这块化石有一条蜗轴状的内弯。

e.en: A {modioliform} shell can confuse beginners.
e.zh: 蜗轴状的贝壳可能让初学者困惑。

modiolus.t: 耳蜗轴；轮毂状中心结构

e.en: The nerve fibers pass through the {modiolus}.
e.zh: 这些神经纤维穿过耳蜗轴。

e.en: The shell's {modiolus} was clearly visible.
e.zh: 贝壳的轮毂状中心清晰可见。

e.en: The countess visited her favorite {modiste}.
e.zh: 伯爵夫人去拜访了她最喜欢的女装裁缝。

e.en: A Paris {modiste} designed the hat.
e.zh: 一位巴黎时装女帽商设计了这顶帽子。

e.en: The system's {modulability} improved after redesign.
e.zh: 重新设计后，系统的可调制性提高了。

e.en: Engineers tested the signal's {modulability}.
e.zh: 工程师测试了该信号的可调制性。

e.en: The team planned the app's {modularization}.
e.zh: 团队规划了这个应用的模块化。

e.en: Good {modularization} makes testing easier.
e.zh: 良好的模块划分会让测试更容易。

e.en: We should {modularize} the old codebase.
e.zh: 我们应该把旧代码库模块化。

e.en: The course was {modularized} into weekly units.
e.zh: 这门课程被按周划分成模块。

e.en: The drug has a {modulatory} effect.
e.zh: 这种药具有调节性的作用。

e.en: Researchers studied {modulatory} signals in the brain.
e.zh: 研究人员研究了大脑中的调制信号。

e.en: Police recognized the thief's {modusoperandi}.
e.zh: 警方认出了这名小偷的惯用手法。

e.en: Secrecy became his {modusoperandi}.
e.zh: 保密成了他的办事方式。

moeurs.t: 风俗习惯；社会道德风气

e.en: The novel satirizes Victorian {moeurs}.
e.zh: 这部小说讽刺了维多利亚时代的社会风气。

e.en: Travelers often misread local {moeurs}.
e.zh: 旅行者常常误解当地的风俗习惯。

e.en: The bread felt {moey} after the rain.
e.zh: 下雨后，面包摸起来潮湿发软。

e.en: His coat was still {moey} inside.
e.zh: 他的外套里面仍然有点潮湿。

moffie.t: 男同性恋贬称；娘娘腔贬称

e.en: He was bullied with the slur {moffie}.
e.zh: 他曾被人用“moffie”这个侮辱词霸凌。

e.en: The film reclaims the word {moffie}.
e.zh: 这部电影重新审视了“moffie”这个词。

e.en: That rude {mofo} stole my seat.
e.zh: 那个粗鲁的混蛋抢了我的座位。

e.en: She is one tough {mofo}.
e.zh: 她真是个特别强悍的家伙。

mofussil.t: 印度乡下地区；外省地方

e.en: He worked in a {mofussil} court.
e.zh: 他曾在印度外省的一家法院工作。

e.en: The newspaper reached many {mofussil} towns.
e.zh: 这份报纸送到了许多外省小镇。

e.en: Our old {mog} sleeps by the fire.
e.zh: 我们家的老猫睡在炉火旁。

e.en: A stray {mog} followed me home.
e.zh: 一只流浪猫跟着我回了家。

e.en: Their {moggy} hates closed doors.
e.zh: 他们家的普通家猫讨厌关着的门。

e.en: A ginger {moggy} sat on the wall.
e.zh: 一只姜黄色的杂种猫坐在墙上。

moghul.t: 莫卧儿人；有权势的大人物

e.en: The palace was built by a {Moghul} emperor.
e.zh: 这座宫殿由一位莫卧儿皇帝建造。

e.en: A media {moghul} bought the channel.
e.zh: 一位传媒大亨买下了这个频道。

e.en: The patient showed signs of {mogilalia}.
e.zh: 这名患者表现出发音困难的迹象。

e.en: Therapy helped reduce her {mogilalia}.
e.zh: 治疗帮助减轻了她的言语障碍。

e.en: The inscription shows a {Moabitish} form of the word.
e.zh: 这段铭文显示了该词的摩押语形式。

e.en: Scholars compared the {Moabitish} customs with Hebrew practices.
e.zh: 学者把摩押人的习俗同希伯来做法相比较。

e.en: A {moanful} wind moved through the empty hall.
e.zh: 一阵悲鸣般的风穿过空荡的大厅。

e.en: Her {moanful} answer ended the cheerful conversation.
e.zh: 她哀怨的回答让愉快的谈话停了下来。

e.en: A {moatlike} ditch surrounded the old farmhouse.
e.zh: 一道像护城河的沟围着那座旧农舍。

e.en: The road formed a {moatlike} barrier around the site.
e.zh: 这条路在场地周围形成了类似护城河的屏障。

e.en: She wore a white {mob-cap} in the kitchen.
e.zh: 她在厨房里戴着一顶白色女式软帽。

e.en: The actor adjusted her {mob-cap} before entering the scene.
e.zh: 演员进场前调整了一下她的家常便帽。

mob-stock.t: 暴民出身；乌合之众血统

e.en: The pamphlet sneered at leaders of {mob-stock}.
e.zh: 那本小册子嘲讽那些出身暴民阶层的领袖。

e.en: He rejected the insult that his family was {mob-stock}.
e.zh: 他拒绝接受说自己家族是乌合之众出身的侮辱。

e.en: The old play calls the servant a {mobaltron}.
e.zh: 那部老戏把仆人称作一个蠢汉。

e.en: Only a {mobaltron} would ignore such plain warnings.
e.zh: 只有迟钝的笨人才会无视这么明显的警告。

e.en: The debate collapsed into {mobbish} shouting.
e.zh: 辩论变成了暴民般的喊叫。

e.en: He disliked the {mobbish} mood of the crowd.
e.zh: 他不喜欢人群那种粗野喧闹的气氛。

e.en: The editor warned against political {mobbism}.
e.zh: 编辑警告不要纵容政治上的群氓主义。

e.en: Their protest turned into sheer {mobbism} after midnight.
e.zh: 午夜后，他们的抗议变成了赤裸裸的暴民行径。

e.en: The mayor called the agitator a dangerous {mobbist}.
e.zh: 市长称那个煽动者是危险的暴民分子。

e.en: A true reformer is not merely a {mobbist}.
e.zh: 真正的改革者并不只是群氓主义者。

e.en: Grandmother kept a lace {mobcap} in the drawer.
e.zh: 祖母把一顶蕾丝女式软帽放在抽屉里。

e.en: The museum displayed a faded {mobcap} from the eighteenth century.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一顶十八世纪褪色的家常便帽。

e.en: The {mobenate} figure stood beside the gate.
e.zh: 那个戴着头巾的人影站在门旁。

e.en: A {mobenate} cloak covered most of his face.
e.zh: 一件带兜帽的斗篷遮住了他大半张脸。

mobese.t: 暴民语言；粗俗群体话语

e.en: The critic dismissed the slogan as pure {mobese}.
e.zh: 评论家把那句口号斥为纯粹的暴民语言。

e.en: Online arguments often sink into angry {mobese}.
e.zh: 网上争论常常陷入愤怒粗俗的群体话语。

e.en: I saved the ticket on my {mobi}.
e.zh: 我把票存在手机上了。

e.en: The article was formatted for a {mobi} reader.
e.zh: 这篇文章被排成适合移动阅读器的格式。

e.en: Her {mobilephone} rang during the meeting.
e.zh: 会议期间她的手机响了。

e.en: Please charge your {mobilephone} before the trip.
e.zh: 出发前请给你的手机充好电。

e.en: The document used {mobilie} as an old spelling of mobile.
e.zh: 这份文件把 mobilie 当作 mobile 的旧拼法使用。

e.en: A {mobilie} force could cross the valley quickly.
e.zh: 一支机动部队能很快穿过山谷。

e.en: The army counted all {mobilizable} reserves before dawn.
e.zh: 军队在黎明前清点了所有可动员的预备力量。

e.en: Only a small budget was {mobilizable} for the project.
e.zh: 这个项目只有一小笔预算可以调动。

mobillette.t: 轻便摩托车；机动脚踏车

e.en: He rode a noisy {mobillette} through the village.
e.zh: 他骑着一辆吵闹的轻便摩托车穿过村子。

e.en: The old {mobillette} needed fuel and a new tire.
e.zh: 那辆旧机动脚踏车需要加油并换个新轮胎。

e.en: The dentist used a {mobilometer} to test the loose tooth.
e.zh: 牙医用活动度测量仪检查那颗松动的牙。

e.en: A {mobilometer} can record small movements in the joint.
e.zh: 活动度测量仪可以记录关节的细微移动。

e.en: The fans became {moblike} after the final whistle.
e.zh: 终场哨响后，球迷变得像暴民一样。

e.en: She feared the {moblike} pressure on the witness.
e.zh: 她担心证人受到群氓式的压力。

e.en: The essay described unchecked populism as {mobocracy}.
e.zh: 这篇文章把失控的民粹主义描述为暴民统治。

e.en: Courts can weaken when {mobocracy} replaces law.
e.zh: 当群氓政治取代法律时，法院可能会被削弱。

e.en: The senator branded his rival a {mobocrat}.
e.zh: 参议员把对手说成暴民政治鼓吹者。

e.en: A {mobocrat} thrives on anger rather than policy.
e.zh: 暴民政治鼓吹者靠愤怒而不是政策得势。

mobocratic.t: 暴民统治的；群氓政治的

e.en: The speech had a strongly {mobocratic} tone.
e.zh: 这场演讲带有强烈的群氓政治色彩。

e.en: They feared a {mobocratic} assault on the courts.
e.zh: 他们担心对法院发起暴民统治式的攻击。

mobot.t: 移动机器人；移动自动装置

e.en: The lab tested a small {mobot} in the hallway.
e.zh: 实验室在走廊里测试了一台小型移动机器人。

e.en: A delivery {mobot} carried medicine across the ward.
e.zh: 一台配送移动机器人把药送过病房。

e.en: She {mogs} through the muddy field every morning.
e.zh: 她每天早晨都艰难地穿过泥泞的田地。

e.en: He {mogs} away at the same dull job.
e.zh: 他一直辛苦地做着同一份乏味的工作。

e.en: The family invited a {mohel} for the ceremony.
e.zh: 这家人请来一位犹太割礼执行者主持仪式。

e.en: A trained {mohel} performed the traditional rite.
e.zh: 一名受过训练的割礼师完成了传统仪式。

e.en: The old desk was made of {mohogany}.
e.zh: 那张旧书桌是用桃花心木做的。

e.en: Her hair had a warm {mohogany} shine.
e.zh: 她的头发泛着温暖的红褐色光泽。

e.en: The collector bought an old {mohur} at auction.
e.zh: 那位收藏家在拍卖会上买了一枚旧莫胡尔金币。

e.en: A gold {mohur} was displayed in the museum case.
e.zh: 一枚莫胡尔金币陈列在博物馆展柜里。

e.en: The strange directions only {moider} me more.
e.zh: 那些奇怪的指示只让我更加困惑。

e.en: Stop {moidering} and answer the question clearly.
e.zh: 别再胡扯了，把问题回答清楚。

e.en: He found a {moidore} among the old coins.
e.zh: 他在一堆旧钱币中发现了一枚葡萄牙旧金币。

e.en: The pirate story mentioned a chest of {moidores}.
e.zh: 那个海盗故事提到了一箱葡萄牙旧金币。

e.en: Workers {moil} in the heat all afternoon.
e.zh: 工人们整个下午都在酷热中辛苦劳作。

e.en: Dark clouds began to {moil} above the hills.
e.zh: 乌云开始在群山上方翻腾。

e.en: They {moiled} in the fields until sunset.
e.zh: 他们在田里辛苦劳作到日落。

e.en: The river {moiled} after the heavy rain.
e.zh: 大雨过后，河水翻腾不息。

e.en: The {moiling} crowd pushed toward the gate.
e.zh: 拥挤翻腾的人群朝大门涌去。

e.en: She spent years {moiling} for very little pay.
e.zh: 她多年辛苦劳作，却只拿到很少的报酬。

e.en: He worked {moilingly} through the long harvest.
e.zh: 他在漫长的收获季里辛苦地干活。

e.en: The smoke rose {moilingly} from the ruined house.
e.zh: 烟雾从废屋中翻腾着升起。

e.en: He {moils} all day in the workshop.
e.zh: 他整天在作坊里辛苦劳作。

e.en: The sea {moils} beneath the winter wind.
e.zh: 冬风之下，大海翻腾不止。

e.en: This corner is the {moistest} part of the basement.
e.zh: 这个角落是地下室里最潮湿的地方。

e.en: Choose the {moistest} cake from the tray.
e.zh: 从托盘里选最湿润的那块蛋糕。

e.en: The garden smelled fresh in the {moistful} air.
e.zh: 花园在湿润的空气中闻起来很清新。

e.en: A {moistful} breeze came off the lake.
e.zh: 一阵湿润的微风从湖面吹来。

e.en: The spray will {moistify} the dry leaves.
e.zh: 喷雾会把干叶子弄湿润。

e.en: Add a little broth to {moistify} the rice.
e.zh: 加一点高汤让米饭更湿润。

e.en: The desert air felt {moistless} and sharp.
e.zh: 沙漠里的空气干燥而刺人。

e.en: His {moistless} cough worried the nurse.
e.zh: 他那种干咳让护士很担心。

e.en: Use {moisture-resistant} paint in the bathroom.
